passages.text: “Bejeweled and all dolled up, wearing flower garlands, scented with sandalwood, I was completely covered with adornments, attended by a following of servants. After taking food and drink, many tasty dishes and a generous amount of grains, I left home, and went to the park. There I had a good time, played around, and then went back to my own house. Since I wanted to see a monastery, I went into Añjana forest at Sāketa. There I saw the Buddha, shedding light on the world. I paid respects and sat down. The Seer taught me the Dhamma out of compassion. After hearing the Great Sage, I penetrated the truth. There I touched the stainless Dhamma, the path to the deathless. Then, because I had become aware of the true Dhamma, I went forth into homelessness. I obtained the three knowledges, the teaching of the Buddha was not in vain.” The Elder Sujātā
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sixes · Verses of the Elder Sujātā
passages.original: “Alaṅkatā suvasanā,  mālinī candanokkhitā;  Sabbābharaṇasañchannā,  dāsīgaṇapurakkhatā.  Annaṁ pānañca ādāya,  khajjaṁ bhojjaṁ anappakaṁ;  Gehato nikkhamitvāna,  uyyānamabhihārayiṁ.  Tattha ramitvā kīḷitvā,  āgacchantī sakaṁ gharaṁ;  Vihāraṁ daṭṭhuṁ pāvisiṁ,  sākete añjanaṁ vanaṁ.  Disvāna lokapajjotaṁ,  vanditvāna upāvisiṁ;  So me dhammamadesesi,  anukampāya cakkhumā.  Sutvā ca kho mahesissa,  saccaṁ sampaṭivijjhahaṁ;  Tattheva virajaṁ dhammaṁ,  phusayiṁ amataṁ padaṁ.  Tato viññātasaddhammā,  pabbajiṁ anagāriyaṁ;  Tisso vijjā anuppattā,  amoghaṁ buddhasāsanan”ti.  … Sujātā therī ….

passages.text: “I was Majjha’s daughter: well-born, with much wealth and property, endowed with beauty. Sons of kings pursued me, sons of wealthy merchants desired me. One sent out a messenger for my father: ‘Give me Anopamā! However much she is worth, your daughter Anopamā, I will give you eight times as much in gold and gems.’ When I saw the Self-Enlightened One, the supreme in the world, the unsurpassable one, I paid homage at his feet, and sat down to one side. Gotama taught me the Dhamma out of compassion. Sitting on that seat, I reached the third fruit. Then I cut off my hair, and went forth into homelessness. Today is the seventh night from when craving was made to wither.” The Elder Anopamā
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sixes · Verses of the Elder Anopamā
passages.original: “Ucce kule ahaṁ jātā,  bahuvitte mahaddhane;  Vaṇṇarūpena sampannā,  dhītā majjhassa atrajā.  Patthitā rājaputtehi,  seṭṭhiputtehi gijjhitā;  Pitu me pesayī dūtaṁ,  detha mayhaṁ anopamaṁ.  Yattakaṁ tulitā esā,  tuyhaṁ dhītā anopamā;  Tato aṭṭhaguṇaṁ dassaṁ,  hiraññaṁ ratanāni ca.  Sāhaṁ disvāna sambuddhaṁ,  lokajeṭṭhaṁ anuttaraṁ;  Tassa pādāni vanditvā,  ekamantaṁ upāvisiṁ.  So me dhammamadesesi,  anukampāya gotamo;  Nisinnā āsane tasmiṁ,  phusayiṁ tatiyaṁ phalaṁ.  Tato kesāni chetvāna,  pabbajiṁ anagāriyaṁ;  Ajja me sattamī ratti,  yato taṇhā visositā”ti.  … Anopamā therī ….

passages.text: “Homage to you, Buddha, Hero! Best of all beings, who released me and many others from suffering. All suffering is fully understood, craving, its cause, has been made to wither, the Eightfold Path has been developed, and I have attained cessation. In the past I was a mother, a child, a father, a brother, and a grandmother. Blind to the truth, I returned again and again, never finding in the darkness what I sought. I have seen the Bhagavant— indeed, this is my last body. Destroyed is rebirth in saṁsāra, now there is no coming back to any state of being. See the disciples on the path— established in energy, self-directed, always making a sincere effort: this is paying homage to the Buddhas! Indeed, for the benefit of many beings, Māyā gave birth to Gotama. Sickness, death, and the mass of suffering are vanquished.” The Elder Mahāpajāpati Gotamī
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sixes · Verses of the Elder Mahāpajāpati Gotamī
passages.original: “Buddha vīra namo tyatthu,  sabbasattānamuttama;  Yo maṁ dukkhā pamocesi,  aññañca bahukaṁ janaṁ.  Sabbadukkhaṁ pariññātaṁ,  Hetutaṇhā visositā;  Bhāvito aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo,  Nirodho phusito mayā.  Mātā putto pitā bhātā,  ayyakā ca pure ahuṁ;  Yathābhuccamajānantī,  saṁsariṁhaṁ anibbisaṁ.  Diṭṭho hi me so bhagavā,  antimoyaṁ samussayo;  Vikkhīṇo jātisaṁsāro,  natthi dāni punabbhavo.  Āraddhavīriye pahitatte,  Niccaṁ daḷhaparakkame;  Samagge sāvake passe,  Esā buddhāna vandanā.  Bahūnaṁ vata atthāya,  Māyā janayi gotamaṁ;  Byādhimaraṇatunnānaṁ,  Dukkhakkhandhaṁ byapānudī”ti.  … Mahāpajāpatigotamī therī ….

passages.text: “Guttā, why did you go forth? You have left behind child, wealth, and all that is dear. Practice in this way, do not be controlled by the mind. Sentient beings are misguided by the mind, enjoying the realm of Māra. Fools wander along in saṁsāra, running through countless births. Interest in sensual pleasures, ill will, attachment to self-identity, clinging to rites and rituals, and the fifth is doubt. Once you abandon these fetters, Bhikkhunī, you will not return to the near shore again. Once you forsake passion, conceit, ignorance, and restlessness, having cut off the fetters, you will bring suffering to an end. Once you have discarded birth in saṁsāra, having fully understood how existence is renewed, seeing the Dhamma, without cravings, you will walk in peace.” The Elder Guttā
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sixes · Verses of the Elder Guttā
passages.original: “Gutte yadatthaṁ pabbajjā,  hitvā puttaṁ vasuṁ piyaṁ;  Tameva anubrūhehi,  mā cittassa vasaṁ gami.  Cittena vañcitā sattā,  mārassa visaye ratā;  Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ,  sandhāvanti aviddasū.  Kāmacchandañca byāpādaṁ,  sakkāyadiṭṭhimeva ca;  Sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ,  vicikicchañca pañcamaṁ.  Saṁyojanāni etāni,  pajahitvāna bhikkhunī;  Orambhāgamanīyāni,  nayidaṁ punarehisi.  Rāgaṁ mānaṁ avijjañca,  uddhaccañca vivajjiya;  Saṁyojanāni chetvāna,  dukkhassantaṁ karissasi.  Khepetvā jātisaṁsāraṁ,  pariññāya punabbhavaṁ;  Diṭṭheva dhamme nicchātā,  upasantā carissatī”ti.  … Guttā therī ….

passages.text: “Four times, five times, I went outside, I had not attained peace of mind, and I had no power over the mind. I approached a bhikkhunī, and respectfully asked questions. She taught me the Dhamma: the elements, the sense domains, the Four Noble Truths, the faculties, the powers, the enlightenment factors, and the Eightfold Path, for the attainment of the highest aim. I heard and followed her instructions. In the first watch of the night, I remembered my previous lives. In the second watch of the night, I purified the divine eye. In the third watch of the night, I destroyed this mass of darkness. Then I dwelled permeating the body with bliss and happiness. On the seventh day I stretched out my feet, I destroyed this mass of darkness.” … The Elder Vijayā The Chapter of the Sixes is finished.
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sixes · Verses of the Elder Vijayā
passages.original: “Catukkhattuṁ pañcakkhattuṁ,  vihārā upanikkhamiṁ;  Aladdhā cetaso santiṁ,  citte avasavattinī.  Bhikkhuniṁ upasaṅkamma,  sakkaccaṁ paripucchahaṁ;  Sā me dhammamadesesi,  dhātuāyatanāni ca.  Cattāri ariyasaccāni,  indriyāni balāni ca;  Bojjhaṅgaṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,  uttamatthassa pattiyā.  Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,  karontī anusāsaniṁ;  Rattiyā purime yāme,  pubbajātimanussariṁ.  Rattiyā majjhime yāme,  dibbacakkhuṁ visodhayiṁ;  Rattiyā pacchime yāme,  tamokhandhaṁ padālayiṁ.  Pītisukhena ca kāyaṁ,  Pharitvā vihariṁ tadā;  Sattamiyā pāde pasāresiṁ,  Tamokhandhaṁ padāliyā”ti.  … Vijayā therī ….  Chakkanipāto niṭṭhito.

passages.text: “With a pestle, young men pound grain. As they nourish wife and children, young men prosper. Work your way through the teaching of the Buddha, and you will have no regrets. Quickly wash your feet, and sit down to one side. Once the mind is well-collected and one-pointed, review all formations as alien, and not as yourself.” “Upon hearing these words, the instructions of Paṭācārā, I washed my feet, and sat down to one side. In the first watch of the night, I remembered my previous lives. In the second watch of the night, I purified the divine eye. In the third watch of the night, I destroyed this mass of darkness. I emerged from that possessing the three knowledges: I did as you instructed. I now possess the three knowledges and am free from influences, and will dwell revering you just as the thirty Devas honor Indra, unconquered in battle.” The Elder Uttarā
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sevens · Verses of the Elder Uttarā
passages.original: “Musalāni gahetvāna,  dhaññaṁ koṭṭenti māṇavā;  Puttadārāni posentā,  dhanaṁ vindanti māṇavā.  Ghaṭetha buddhasāsane,  yaṁ katvā nānutappati;  Khippaṁ pādāni dhovitvā,  ekamantaṁ nisīdatha.  Cittaṁ upaṭṭhapetvāna,  ekaggaṁ susamāhitaṁ;  Paccavekkhatha saṅkhāre,  parato no ca attato”.  “Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,  paṭācārānusāsaniṁ;  Pāde pakkhālayitvāna,  ekamante upāvisiṁ.  Rattiyā purime yāme,  pubbajātimanussariṁ;  Rattiyā majjhime yāme,  dibbacakkhuṁ visodhayiṁ.  Rattiyā pacchime yāme,  tamokhandhaṁ padālayiṁ;  Tevijjā atha vuṭṭhāsiṁ,  katā te anusāsanī.  Sakkaṁva devā tidasā,  saṅgāme aparājitaṁ;  Purakkhatvā vihassāmi,  tevijjāmhi anāsavā”.  … Uttarā therī ….

passages.text: “I am a bhikkhunī with well-developed spiritual powers. I established mindfulness, and mastered the path of peace, the joyful pacification of formations.” “On whose account did you shave your head? You seem like a contemplative, but you disapprove of dogmas; why do you roam around confused?” “Those who follow dogmas rely on their views. They do not know the Dhamma; they are not masters of the Dhamma. But the one who was born in the Sakyan clan, the unrivaled Buddha, taught me the Dhamma that transcends views: suffering, the origin of suffering, the overcoming of suffering, and the Noble Eightfold Path leading to the appeasement of suffering. After I heard his words, I dwelled devoted to the teaching. I obtained the three knowledges, and completed the teaching of the Buddha. In this way all fixation is annihilated, and the mass of darkness destroyed. Thus be aware, Wicked One, Death—you are destroyed!”
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sevens · Verses of the Elder Cālā
passages.original: “Satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvāna,  bhikkhunī bhāvitindriyā;  Paṭivijjhi padaṁ santaṁ,  saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ”.  “Kaṁ nu uddissa muṇḍāsi,  samaṇī viya dissasi;  Na ca rocesi pāsaṇḍe,  kimidaṁ carasi momuhā”.  “Ito bahiddhā pāsaṇḍā,  diṭṭhiyo upanissitā;  Na te dhammaṁ vijānanti,  na te dhammassa kovidā.  Atthi sakyakule jāto,  buddho appaṭipuggalo;  So me dhammamadesesi,  diṭṭhīnaṁ samatikkamaṁ.  Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ,  Dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ;  Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,  Dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.  Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,  vihariṁ sāsane ratā;  Tisso vijjā anuppattā,  kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ.  Sabbattha vihatā nandī,  tamokhandho padālito;  Evaṁ jānāhi pāpima,  nihato tvamasi antaka”.

passages.text: The Elder Cālā
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sevens · Verses of the Elder Cālā

passages.text: “I am mindful and of clear sight, a bhikkhunī with well-developed spiritual powers. I mastered the path of peace that is not practiced by vile people.” “Why don’t you appreciate being born? When one is born, one enjoys sensual pleasures. Enjoy the delights of sensual pleasures, do not regret it later.” “From birth there is death, the severing of hands and feet, flogging, imprisonment, and hardship; when one is born, one undergoes suffering. But the one who is born in the Sakyan clan, Self-Enlightened and Unconquered, taught me the Dhamma that transcends birth; Suffering, the origin of suffering, the overcoming of suffering, and the Noble Eightfold Path leading to the appeasement of suffering. After I heard his words, I dwelled devoted to the teaching. I obtained the three knowledges, and completed the teaching of the Buddha. In this way all fixation is annihilated, the mass of darkness destroyed. Thus be aware, Wicked One, Death—you are destroyed!”
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Sevens · Verses of the Elder Upacālā
passages.original: “Satimatī cakkhumatī,  bhikkhunī bhāvitindriyā;  Paṭivijjhi padaṁ santaṁ,  akāpurisasevitaṁ”.  “Kiṁ nu jātiṁ na rocesi,  jāto kāmāni bhuñjati;  Bhuñjāhi kāmaratiyo,  māhu pacchānutāpinī”.  “Jātassa maraṇaṁ hoti,  hatthapādāna chedanaṁ;  Vadhabandhapariklesaṁ,  jāto dukkhaṁ nigacchati.  Atthi sakyakule jāto,  sambuddho aparājito;  So me dhammamadesesi,  jātiyā samatikkamaṁ.  Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ,  dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ;  Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,  dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.  Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,  vihariṁ sāsane ratā;  Tisso vijjā anuppattā,  kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ.  Sabbattha vihatā nandī,  tamokhandho padālito;  Evaṁ jānāhi pāpima,  nihato tvamasi antaka”.

passages.text: “I am a bhikkhunī with perfect morality, with sense faculties well restrained; I attained the path of peace, sweet like nectar.” “You used to dwell amongst the Tāvatiṃsa, Yāmā, and Tusitā Devas, the Nimmānarati Devas, and the Vasavatti Devas. Aspire the mind towards where you dwelt formerly.” “The Tāvatiṃsa, Yāmā, and Tusitā Devas, the Nimmānarati Devas, and the Vasavatti Devas— time after time, one existence after the other, their first concern is themselves. They have not gone beyond selfhood; they wander between birth and death. The entire world is ablaze, the entire world is burning, the entire world is in flames, the entire world is shaking. The unshakable, unmatched Dhamma, not practiced by ordinary people, is what the Buddha taught, and that is what my mind enjoys. After I heard his words, I dwelled devoted to the teaching. I obtained the three knowledges, and completed the teaching of the Buddha.
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Eights · Verses of the Elder Sīsūpacālā
passages.original: “Bhikkhunī sīlasampannā,  indriyesu susaṁvutā;  Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ,  asecanakamojavaṁ”.  “Tāvatiṁsā ca yāmā ca,  tusitā cāpi devatā;  Nimmānaratino devā,  ye devā vasavattino;  Tattha cittaṁ paṇīdhehi,  yattha te vusitaṁ pure”.  “Tāvatiṁsā ca yāmā ca,  tusitā cāpi devatā;  Nimmānaratino devā,  ye devā vasavattino.  Kālaṁ kālaṁ bhavābhavaṁ,  sakkāyasmiṁ purakkhatā;  Avītivattā sakkāyaṁ,  jātimaraṇasārino.  Sabbo ādīpito loko,  sabbo loko padīpito;  Sabbo pajjalito loko,  sabbo loko pakampito.  Akampiyaṁ atuliyaṁ,  aputhujjanasevitaṁ;  Buddho dhammamadesesi,  tattha me nirato mano.  Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,  vihariṁ sāsane ratā;  Tisso vijjā anuppattā,  kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ.

passages.text: In this way all fixation is annihilated, the mass of darkness destroyed. Thus be aware, Wicked One, Death—you are destroyed!” … The Elder Sīsūpacālā The Chapter of the Eights is finished.
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Eights · Verses of the Elder Sīsūpacālā
passages.original: Sabbattha vihatā nandī,  tamokhandho padālito;  Evaṁ jānāhi pāpima,  nihato tvamasi antaka”.  … Sīsūpacālā therī ….  Aṭṭhakanipāto niṭṭhito.

passages.text: “Vaḍḍha, do not get caught in the endless thicket of the world. Oh little child, do not take part in suffering again and again. Vaḍḍha, the sages dwell easily, carefree and free from doubt. They have become cool and tamed, and abide free from influences. That path walked by the seers who have attained vision, leading to the end of suffering: Vaḍḍha, devote yourself to that!” “Mother, you speak from a place of self-confidence. I suspect, mom, there is no thicket to be found in you.” “Vaḍḍha, not even the slightest thicket, based on any conditions, whether inferior, superior, or in the middle, can be found in me. I have destroyed all influences by meditating with heedfulness. I obtained the three knowledges, and completed the teaching of the Buddha.” “Surely, my mother spurred me with a noble goad, with these compassionate verses, of the highest benefit. After I heard her words, instructed by my mother, I was met with a sense of urgency to practice the Dhamma for the attainment of safety from bondage.
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Nines · Verses of the Elder Vaḍḍha’s Mother
passages.original: “Mā su te vaḍḍha lokamhi,  vanatho āhu kudācanaṁ;  Mā puttaka punappunaṁ,  ahu dukkhassa bhāgimā.  Sukhañhi vaḍḍha munayo,  anejā chinnasaṁsayā;  Sītibhūtā damappattā,  viharanti anāsavā.  Tehānuciṇṇaṁ isībhi,  maggaṁ dassanapattiyā;  Dukkhassantakiriyāya,  tvaṁ vaḍḍha anubrūhaya”.  “Visāradāva bhaṇasi,  etamatthaṁ janetti me;  Maññāmi nūna māmike,  vanatho te na vijjati”.  “Ye keci vaḍḍha saṅkhārā,  hīnā ukkaṭṭhamajjhimā;  Aṇūpi aṇumattopi,  vanatho me na vijjati.  Sabbe me āsavā khīṇā,  appamattassa jhāyato;  Tisso vijjā anuppattā,  kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ”.  “Uḷāraṁ vata me mātā,  patodaṁ samavassari;  Paramatthasañhitā gāthā,  yathāpi anukampikā.  Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,  anusiṭṭhiṁ janettiyā;  Dhammasaṁvegamāpādiṁ,  yogakkhemassa pattiyā.

passages.text: With a mind bent upon striving, active by day and by night, being exhorted by my mother, I touched the highest peace.” … The Elder Vaḍḍha’s Mother The Chapter of the Nines is finished.
passages.title: Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs · Chapter of the Nines · Verses of the Elder Vaḍḍha’s Mother
passages.original: Sohaṁ padhānapahitatto,  rattindivamatandito;  Mātarā codito santo,  aphusiṁ santimuttamaṁ”.  … Vaḍḍhamātā therī ….  Navakanipāto niṭṭhito.

passages.text: All things are preceded by the mind, surpassed by the mind, created by the mind. If one speaks or acts with a corrupted mind, Then suffering follows, As a track follows a wheel.
passages.title: Dhammapada 1 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā,  manoseṭṭhā manomayā;  Manasā ce paduṭṭhena,  bhāsati vā karoti vā;  Tato naṁ dukkhamanveti,  cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ.

passages.text: All things are preceded by the mind, surpassed by the mind, created by the mind. If one speaks or acts with a pure mind, Then happiness follows, As a shadow that never leaves.
passages.title: Dhammapada 2 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā,  manoseṭṭhā manomayā;  Manasā ce pasannena,  bhāsati vā karoti vā;  Tato naṁ sukhamanveti,  chāyāva anapāyinī.

passages.text: “They abused me, they hurt me, they defeated me, they robbed me!” For those who hold on to this hostility is never replaced by peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 3 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ,  ajini maṁ ahāsi me;  Ye ca taṁ upanayhanti,  veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.

passages.text: “They abused me, they hurt me, they defeated me, they robbed me!” For those who do not hold on to this hostility is replaced by peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 4 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ,  ajini maṁ ahāsi me;  Ye ca taṁ nupanayhanti,  veraṁ tesūpasammati.

passages.text: Hostility is never pacified by means of hostility. Only by means of non-hostility is it pacified. This is an eternal truth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 5 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Na hi verena verāni,  sammantīdha kudācanaṁ;  Averena ca sammanti,  esa dhammo sanantano.

passages.text: Others do not know that we must be restrained. The wise ones who know this attain peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 6 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Pare ca na vijānanti,  mayamettha yamāmase;  Ye ca tattha vijānanti,  tato sammanti medhagā.

passages.text: If one focuses on beauty, lacks sense-restraint, does not know the right amount when eating, is lazy, and lacks energy, Māra subdues such a person just as the wind subdues a weak tree.
passages.title: Dhammapada 7 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ,  indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ;  Bhojanamhi cāmattaññuṁ,  kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ;  Taṁ ve pasahati māro,  vāto rukkhaṁva dubbalaṁ.

passages.text: If one does not focus on beauty, has good sense-restraint, knows the right amount when eating, has faith, and has persistent energy, Māra does not subdue such a person just as the wind does not subdue a stone mountain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 8 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ,  Indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ;  Bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ,  Saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ;  Taṁ ve nappasahati māro,  Vāto selaṁva pabbataṁ.

passages.text: An impure person who dons a monastic robe without true self-control is not worthy of the monastic robe.
passages.title: Dhammapada 9 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ,  yo vatthaṁ paridahissati;  Apeto damasaccena,  na so kāsāvamarahati.

passages.text: One who has expelled all impurity, is focused on moral conduct, and is committed to true self-control is worthy of the monastic robe.
passages.title: Dhammapada 10 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Yo ca vantakasāvassa,  sīlesu susamāhito;  Upeto damasaccena,  sa ve kāsāvamarahati.

passages.text: One who thinks the non-essential is essential and who sees the essential as non-essential does not arrive at the essence; their conduct is based on incorrect attitudes.
passages.title: Dhammapada 11 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Asāre sāramatino,  sāre cāsāradassino;  Te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti,  micchāsaṅkappagocarā.

passages.text: One who knows the essential as essential and the non-essential as non-essential arrives at the essence; their conduct is based on correct attitudes.
passages.title: Dhammapada 12 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Sārañca sārato ñatvā,  asārañca asārato;  Te sāraṁ adhigacchanti,  sammāsaṅkappagocarā.

passages.text: Just as rain penetrates a poorly sealed house, in the same way, passion penetrates an undeveloped mind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 13 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ,  vuṭṭhī samativijjhati;  Evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ,  rāgo samativijjhati.

passages.text: Just as rain does not penetrate a well-sealed house, in the same way, passion does not penetrate a well-developed mind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 14 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Yathā agāraṁ suchannaṁ,  vuṭṭhī na samativijjhati;  Evaṁ subhāvitaṁ cittaṁ,  rāgo na samativijjhati.

passages.text: One sorrows here, one sorrows afterwards, an evildoer sorrows both times. One sorrows and agonizes after seeing one's own defiled actions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 15 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Idha socati pecca socati,  Pāpakārī ubhayattha socati;  So socati so vihaññati,  Disvā kammakiliṭṭhamattano.

passages.text: One rejoices here, one rejoices afterwards, one who has made merit rejoices both times. One rejoices and exults after seeing one's own pure actions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 16 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Idha modati pecca modati,  Katapuñño ubhayattha modati;  So modati so pamodati,  Disvā kammavisuddhimattano.

passages.text: Tormented here, tormented afterwards, an evildoer is tormented both times. One is tormented by the thought “I have done evil,” And one is tormented even more when one has arrived at a bad destiny.
passages.title: Dhammapada 17 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Idha tappati pecca tappati,  Pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati;  “Pāpaṁ me katan”ti tappati,  Bhiyyo tappati duggatiṁ gato.

passages.text: One delights here, one delights afterwards, one who has made merit delights both times. One is delighted by the thought “I have made merit,” And one delights even more when one has arrived at a good destiny.
passages.title: Dhammapada 18 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Idha nandati pecca nandati,  Katapuñño ubhayattha nandati;  “Puññaṁ me katan”ti nandati,  Bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.

passages.text: A negligent person who says much that is beneficial but does not act accordingly is like a cowherd who counts other people's cows, and is not part of the contemplative life.
passages.title: Dhammapada 19 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Bahumpi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno,  Na takkaro hoti naro pamatto;  Gopova gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ,  Na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.

passages.text: Even if they say little that is beneficial, one who lives according to the Dhamma, having abandoned passion, hatred, and delusion, with accurate understanding and a well-liberated mind, not grasping either here or beyond, is part of the contemplative life.
passages.title: Dhammapada 20 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Pairs
passages.original: Appampi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno,  Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī;  Rāgañca dosañca pahāya mohaṁ,  Sammappajāno suvimuttacitto;  Anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā,  Sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.

passages.text: Rather than a thousand sayings not connected to the goal, it is better to have just one sentence about the goal if one reaches peace after hearing it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 100 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Sahassamapi ce vācā,  anatthapadasaṁhitā;  Ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo,  yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

passages.text: Rather than a thousand poems not connected to the goal, it is better to have just one line of a poem if one reaches peace after hearing it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 101 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Sahassamapi ce gāthā,  anatthapadasaṁhitā;  Ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo,  yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

passages.text: One might utter a hundred poems not connected to the goal; it is better to have just one line of Dhamma if one reaches peace after hearing it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 102 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca gāthā sataṁ bhāse,  anatthapadasaṁhitā;  Ekaṁ dhammapadaṁ seyyo,  yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

passages.text: One might subjugate a million people in battle, but one who subjugates oneself has won the ultimate victory.
passages.title: Dhammapada 103 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena,  saṅgāme mānuse jine;  Ekañca jeyyamattānaṁ,  sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.

passages.text: It is better to subjugate yourself than other people, for one who is self-trained always acts with restraint.
passages.title: Dhammapada 104 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Attā have jitaṁ seyyo,  yā cāyaṁ itarā pajā;  Attadantassa posassa,  niccaṁ saññatacārino.

passages.text: No angel or fairy, demon or god, can turn such a person’s victory into defeat.
passages.title: Dhammapada 105 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Neva devo na gandhabbo,  na māro saha brahmunā;  Jitaṁ apajitaṁ kayirā,  tathārūpassa jantuno.

passages.text: Every month one might conduct a hundred sacrifices worth thousands; Or for a single moment one could pay homage to a self-developed person. That homage is better than a hundred years of sacrifices.
passages.title: Dhammapada 106 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Māse māse sahassena,  yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ;  Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ,  muhuttamapi pūjaye;  Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo,  yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.

passages.text: One might spend a hundred years tending to a fire in a forest; or for a single moment one could pay homage to a self-developed person. That homage is better than a hundred years of sacrifices.
passages.title: Dhammapada 107 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jantu,  aggiṁ paricare vane;  Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ,  muhuttamapi pūjaye;  Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo,  yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.

passages.text: One could make any kind of offering or sacrifice in the world for a year, pursuing merit; but all of that is not even a quarter as good as honoring those who are upright.
passages.title: Dhammapada 108 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ va hutaṁ va loke,  Saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho;  Sabbampi taṁ na catubhāgameti,  Abhivādanā ujjugatesu seyyo.

passages.text: For one who is virtuous, respectful, and always reverential towards the elderly, four things increase: vitality, beauty, pleasure, and strength.
passages.title: Dhammapada 109 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Abhivādanasīlissa,  niccaṁ vuḍḍhāpacāyino;  Cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti,  āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.

passages.text: Better than living for a hundred years without virtue and concentration, is living for one day as a virtuous meditator.
passages.title: Dhammapada 110 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  dussīlo asamāhito;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  sīlavantassa jhāyino.

passages.text: Better than living for a hundred years without wisdom and concentration, is living for one day as a wise meditator.
passages.title: Dhammapada 111 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  duppañño asamāhito;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  paññavantassa jhāyino.

passages.text: Better than living for a hundred years with laziness and indolence, is living for one day with determination and resolve.
passages.title: Dhammapada 112 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  kusīto hīnavīriyo;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  vīriyamārabhato daḷhaṁ.

passages.text: Better than living for a hundred years without seeing arising and vanishing, is living for one day while seeing arising and vanishing.
passages.title: Dhammapada 113 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  passato udayabbayaṁ.

passages.text: Better than living for a hundred years without seeing the path to the deathless, is living for one day while seeing the path to the deathless.
passages.title: Dhammapada 114 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  passato amataṁ padaṁ.

passages.text: Better than living for a hundred years without seeing the ultimate truth, is living for one day while seeing the ultimate truth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 115 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  apassaṁ dhammamuttamaṁ;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  passato dhammamuttamaṁ.

passages.text: Rush to do good, keep the mind back from evil. One who is slow to do good appreciates evil.
passages.title: Dhammapada 116 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe,  pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye;  Dandhañhi karoto puññaṁ,  pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.

passages.text: If a person does something evil they should not do it again. Take no interest in it; the accumulation of evil is suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 117 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Pāpañce puriso kayirā,  Na naṁ kayirā punappunaṁ;  Na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha,  Dukkho pāpassa uccayo.

passages.text: If a person does something good they should do it again. Take an interest in it; the accumulation of merit is pleasant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 118 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Puññañce puriso kayirā,  kayirā naṁ punappunaṁ;  Tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha,  sukho puññassa uccayo.

passages.text: One sees evil as good as long as its results have yet to fully manifest; but when the results of that evil fully manifest, then one sees evil as evil.
passages.title: Dhammapada 119 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Pāpopi passati bhadraṁ,  Yāva pāpaṁ na paccati;  Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ,  Atha pāpo pāpāni passati.

passages.text: One sees good as evil as long as its results have yet to fully manifest; but when the results of that good fully manifest, then one sees good as good.
passages.title: Dhammapada 120 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Bhadropi passati pāpaṁ,  Yāva bhadraṁ na paccati;  Yadā ca paccati bhadraṁ,  Atha bhadro bhadrāni passati.

passages.text: Do not disregard evil, thinking it will have no consequence. Just as falling drops of water fill up a bucket, a fool becomes full of evil collecting it little by little.
passages.title: Dhammapada 121 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Māvamaññetha pāpassa,  na mantaṁ āgamissati;  Udabindunipātena,  udakumbhopi pūrati;  Bālo pūrati pāpassa,  thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.

passages.text: Do not disregard merit, thinking it will have no consequence. Just as falling drops of water fill up a bucket, a sage becomes full of merit collecting it little by little.
passages.title: Dhammapada 122 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Māvamaññetha puññassa,  na mandaṁ āgamissati;  Udabindunipātena,  udakumbhopi pūrati;  Dhīro pūrati puññassa,  thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.

passages.text: Just as a wealthy merchant with little protection avoids a dangerous road, just as one who wishes to live avoids poison, one should avoid evil.
passages.title: Dhammapada 123 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Vāṇijova bhayaṁ maggaṁ,  appasattho mahaddhano;  Visaṁ jīvitukāmova,  pāpāni parivajjaye.

passages.text: If a hand is unwounded then it can take away poison; poison cannot affect one who has no wound. No evil comes to one who does none.
passages.title: Dhammapada 124 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa,  hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ;  Nābbaṇaṁ visamanveti,  natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.

passages.text: If one abuses a faultless, pure, and flawless person, then evil will come back to that fool, like fine dust thrown against the wind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 125 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Yo appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati,  Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa;  Tameva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ,  Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁva khitto.

passages.text: Some people arise in wombs; evildoers, in hell; those on the right course go to heaven; the uncorrupted attain Nibbāna.
passages.title: Dhammapada 126 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Gabbhameke uppajjanti,  nirayaṁ pāpakammino;  Saggaṁ sugatino yanti,  parinibbanti anāsavā.

passages.text: Not by going into the sky, or into the ocean, or into a mountain cleft, or anywhere in the world, can one find a place where one is free from one’s evil deeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 127 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe,  Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa;  Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso,  Yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā.

passages.text: Not by going into the sky, or into the ocean, or into a mountain cleft, or anywhere in the world, can one find a place where one is not caught by death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 128 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of Evil
passages.original: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe,  Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa;  Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso,  Yatthaṭṭhitaṁ nappasaheyya maccu.

passages.text: Everyone dreads violence, everyone fears death; recognizing that you are similar, do not harm or cause others to harm.
passages.title: Dhammapada 129 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa,  sabbe bhāyanti maccuno;  Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā,  na haneyya na ghātaye.

passages.text: Everyone dreads violence, everyone likes to live; recognizing that you are similar, do not harm or cause others to harm.
passages.title: Dhammapada 130 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa,  sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ;  Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā,  na haneyya na ghātaye.

passages.text: Beings want pleasure; if one harms them with violence while seeking pleasure for oneself, one will find no pleasure in the future.
passages.title: Dhammapada 131 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni,  yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati;  Attano sukhamesāno,  pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Beings want pleasure; if one does not harm them with violence while seeking pleasure for oneself, one will find pleasure in the future.
passages.title: Dhammapada 132 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni,  yo daṇḍena na hiṁsati;  Attano sukhamesāno,  pecca so labhate sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Say no harsh words to anyone; they might respond in kind. Hostile speech is painful, and it may provoke a violent response.
passages.title: Dhammapada 133 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci,  vuttā paṭivadeyyu taṁ;  Dukkhā hi sārambhakathā,  paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu taṁ.

passages.text: If you are non-reactive, like a broken bell, then you have reached Nibbāna and no conflict can be found in you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 134 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Sace neresi attānaṁ,  kaṁso upahato yathā;  Esa pattosi nibbānaṁ,  sārambho te na vijjati.

passages.text: Just as a cowherd, using a stick, herds cattle through a pasture, in the same way, decrepitude and death herd the living through life.
passages.title: Dhammapada 135 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo,  gāvo pājeti gocaraṁ;  Evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca,  āyuṁ pājenti pāṇinaṁ.

passages.text: Performing evil actions, a fool does not attain awakening. The unwise person is tormented by those actions as if burned by fire.
passages.title: Dhammapada 136 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Atha pāpāni kammāni,  karaṁ bālo na bujjhati;  Sehi kammehi dummedho,  aggidaḍḍhova tappati.

passages.text: One who is violent towards the nonviolent, one who harms the harmless, will soon experience one of ten consequences:
passages.title: Dhammapada 137 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu,  appaduṭṭhesu dussati;  Dasannamaññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ,  khippameva nigacchati.

passages.text: Harsh sensations, deprivation, physical injury, severe illness, mental derangement,
passages.title: Dhammapada 138 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Vedanaṁ pharusaṁ jāniṁ,  sarīrassa va bhedanaṁ;  Garukaṁ vāpi ābādhaṁ,  cittakkhepaṁ va pāpuṇe.

passages.text: legal trouble, severe accusations, loss of relatives, dissipation of wealth,
passages.title: Dhammapada 139 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Rājato vā upasaggaṁ,  Abbhakkhānaṁ va dāruṇaṁ;  Parikkhayaṁ va ñātīnaṁ,  Bhogānaṁ va pabhaṅguraṁ.

passages.text: or their house catching on fire. Then, when the fool is separated from their body, they will reappear in hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 140 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Atha vāssa agārāni,  aggi ḍahati pāvako;  Kāyassa bhedā duppañño,  nirayaṁ sopapajjati.

passages.text: Nudity, tangled hair, filth, fasting, sleeping on the ground, squatting in the mud - these cannot purify a mortal who has not yet gone beyond doubt.
passages.title: Dhammapada 141 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā,  Nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā;  Rajojallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ,  Sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.

passages.text: However, if one who wears adornments is well-behaved, peaceful, restrained, committed to spiritual practice, and has renounced violence towards all beings, then they are a saint, a contemplative, a monk.
passages.title: Dhammapada 142 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Alaṅkato cepi samaṁ careyya,  Santo danto niyato brahmacārī;  Sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṁ,  So brāhmaṇo so samaṇo sa bhikkhu.

passages.text: What person can be found in this world that is restrained by conscience? Who wakes up when criticized, like a fine horse struck by a whip?
passages.title: Dhammapada 143 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Hirīnisedho puriso,  koci lokasmi vijjati;  Yo niddaṁ apabodheti,  asso bhadro kasāmiva.

passages.text: Like a fine horse struck by a whip, be ardent and filled with urgency. By means of faith, virtue, determination, concentration, investigation of Dhamma, perfect knowledge, perfect conduct, and thorough awareness, abandon this immense suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 144 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho,  Ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha;  Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca,  Samādhinā dhammavinicchayena ca;  Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā,  Jahissatha dukkhamidaṁ anappakaṁ.

passages.text: Irrigators guide water, fletchers shape arrows, carpenters shape wood, those who practice well train themselves.
passages.title: Dhammapada 145 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Violence
passages.original: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā,  Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ;  Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā,  Attānaṁ damayanti subbatā.

passages.text: Who can laugh, who can delight, since this is always on fire? Obscured by darkness, you do not search for light.
passages.title: Dhammapada 146 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Ko nu hāso kimānando,  niccaṁ pajjalite sati;  Andhakārena onaddhā,  padīpaṁ na gavesatha.

passages.text: See that the mind has been made a puppet, damaged with arrogance, afflicted with excessive thought, lacking stability and composure.
passages.title: Dhammapada 147 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ,  arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ;  Āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ,  yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.

passages.text: This body is decrepit, fragile, a nest of disease, a putrid heap that falls apart, since life ends in death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 148 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Parijiṇṇamidaṁ rūpaṁ,  roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ;  Bhijjati pūtisandeho,  maraṇantañhi jīvitaṁ.

passages.text: Set aside like gourds in autumn - when seeing these faded bones, what appreciation can there be?
passages.title: Dhammapada 149 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Yānimāni apatthāni,  alābūneva sārade;  Kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni,  tāni disvāna kā rati.

passages.text: Like a city made of bones, wrapped in meat and blood, a place of decay and death, conceit and contempt.
passages.title: Dhammapada 150 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ,  maṁsalohitalepanaṁ;  Yattha jarā ca maccu ca,  māno makkho ca ohito.

passages.text: Even splendid royal chariots wear out; so too, this body decays. But the true Dhamma never decays: it is made known by those who are peaceful and virtuous.
passages.title: Dhammapada 151 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā,  Atho sarīrampi jaraṁ upeti;  Satañca dhammo na jaraṁ upeti,  Santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.

passages.text: A person who has learned little ages like an ox: their muscles grow but their wisdom does not.
passages.title: Dhammapada 152 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Appassutāyaṁ puriso,  balībaddhova jīrati;  Maṁsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti,  paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Wandering through many lives, seeking but not finding the builder of this house - repeatedly experiencing the suffering of birth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 153 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ,  sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ;  Gahakāraṁ gavesanto,  dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.

passages.text: House-builder, you have been seen! You will build no house again. All your rafters are broken, the roof-peak dismantled. The mind has gone to the unconditioned - the elimination of craving has been reached.
passages.title: Dhammapada 154 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi,  puna gehaṁ na kāhasi;  Sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā,  gahakūṭaṁ visaṅkhataṁ;  Visaṅkhāragataṁ cittaṁ,  taṇhānaṁ khayamajjhagā.

passages.text: Those who have neither lived a spiritual life nor acquired wealth during their youth, Waste away like old herons by a fishless pond.
passages.title: Dhammapada 155 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ,  aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ;  Jiṇṇakoñcāva jhāyanti,  khīṇamaccheva pallale.

passages.text: Those who have neither lived a spiritual life nor acquired wealth during their youth, lay around like wasted arrows, lamenting the past.
passages.title: Dhammapada 156 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Decay
passages.original: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ,  aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ;  Senti cāpātikhīṇāva,  purāṇāni anutthunaṁ.

passages.text: If one values oneself, then one should guard oneself well; during any of the three phases of the night, a wise person should remain alert.
passages.title: Dhammapada 157 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attānañce piyaṁ jaññā,  rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ;  Tiṇṇaṁ aññataraṁ yāmaṁ,  paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.

passages.text: First one should settles oneself in what is proper, then one may instruct others; a wise person should not become defiled.
passages.title: Dhammapada 158 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attānameva paṭhamaṁ,  patirūpe nivesaye;  Athaññamanusāseyya,  na kilisseyya paṇḍito.

passages.text: One should act the same way that one instructs others to act; one who is well-trained can train others - for it is truly hard to train oneself.
passages.title: Dhammapada 159 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attānañce tathā kayirā,  yathāññamanusāsati;  Sudanto vata dametha,  attā hi kira duddamo.

passages.text: One is one’s own protector - how could another protect you? One who has trained oneself well has acquired a protector that is truly hard to acquire.
passages.title: Dhammapada 160 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attā hi attano nātho,  ko hi nātho paro siyā;  Attanā hi sudantena,  nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.

passages.text: Evil is done by oneself, born from oneself, produced by oneself; in this way a fool self-destructs, like a diamond cutting through stone.
passages.title: Dhammapada 161 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ,  Attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ;  Abhimatthati dummedhaṁ,  Vajiraṁvasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.

passages.text: One who is excessively immoral, like a tree overgrown by vines, does to oneself what an enemy wants.
passages.title: Dhammapada 162 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Yassa accantadussilyaṁ,  māluvā sālamivotthataṁ;  Karoti so tathattānaṁ,  yathā naṁ icchatī diso.

passages.text: It is easy to do things that are worthless and of no benefit to oneself; but to do what is beneficial and worthwhile is extremely difficult.
passages.title: Dhammapada 163 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Sukarāni asādhūni,  attano ahitāni ca;  Yaṁ ve hitañca sādhuñca,  taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.

passages.text: A foolish person who, based on a harmful perspective, reviles the teachings of the Worthy One, brings about their own destruction like a monocarpic plant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 164 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ,  ariyānaṁ dhammajīvinaṁ;  Paṭikkosati dummedho,  diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ;  Phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva,  attaghātāya phallati.

passages.text: By oneself evil is done, by oneself one becomes defiled; by oneself evil is not done, by oneself one becomes purified; purity and impurity depend on oneself - no one can purify another.
passages.title: Dhammapada 165 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ,  attanā saṅkilissati;  Attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ,  attanāva visujjhati;  Suddhī asuddhi paccattaṁ,  nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.

passages.text: One should not abandon one’s own welfare for the sake of others, no matter how many; having understood one’s own welfare, one should be intent upon it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 166 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Self
passages.original: Attadatthaṁ paratthena,  bahunāpi na hāpaye;  Attadatthamabhiññāya,  sadatthapasuto siyā.

passages.text: One should not participate in inferior teachings, one should not live negligently, one should not participate in wrong view, one should not increase worldliness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 167 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya,  pamādena na saṁvase;  Micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya,  na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.

passages.text: One should apply effort, one should not be negligent, one should practice Dhamma well; one who practices the Dhamma rests happily, in this world and the next.
passages.title: Dhammapada 168 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya,  dhammaṁ sucaritaṁ care;  Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

passages.text: One should practice Dhamma well, one should not engage in misconduct; one who practices the Dhamma rests happily, in this world and the next.
passages.title: Dhammapada 169 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ,  na naṁ duccaritaṁ care;  Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

passages.text: Like seeing a bubble, like seeing a mirage - one who regards the world in this way is not seen by the Lord of Death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 170 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Yathā pubbuḷakaṁ passe,  yathā passe marīcikaṁ;  Evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ,  maccurājā na passati.

passages.text: Come, look at this world, as splendid as a royal chariot, where fools become immersed, but the conscious do not stick.
passages.title: Dhammapada 171 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ,  cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ;  Yattha bālā visīdanti,  natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.

passages.text: One who previously was negligent but now is not illuminates this world like the moon set free from a cloud.
passages.title: Dhammapada 172 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Yo ca pubbe pamajjitvā,  pacchā so nappamajjati;  Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti,  abbhā muttova candimā.

passages.text: One who replaces their evil deeds with wholesome ones illuminates this world like the moon set free from a cloud.
passages.title: Dhammapada 173 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ,  kusalena pidhīyati;  Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti,  abbhā muttova candimā.

passages.text: This world has become blind; rare are those who see clearly. Like a bird freed from a net, few go to heaven.
passages.title: Dhammapada 174 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Andhabhūto ayaṁ loko,  tanukettha vipassati;  Sakuṇo jālamuttova,  appo saggāya gacchati.

passages.text: Like swans moving through the air, like mystics moving through the sky, the wise leave this world, having defeated Māra and his army.
passages.title: Dhammapada 175 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti,  ākāse yanti iddhiyā;  Nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā,  jetvā māraṁ savāhiniṁ.

passages.text: There is no evil that cannot be done by one who tells lies and disregards the afterlife.
passages.title: Dhammapada 176 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa,  musāvādissa jantuno;  Vitiṇṇaparalokassa,  natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.

passages.text: Stingy fools, those who do not praise giving, do not go the deva-world. The wise rejoice in giving, and because of that they are happy hereafter.
passages.title: Dhammapada 177 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Na ve kadariyā devalokaṁ vajanti,  Bālā have nappasaṁsanti dānaṁ;  Dhīro ca dānaṁ anumodamāno,  Teneva so hoti sukhī parattha.

passages.text: Compared to being the sole ruler of the earth, or going to heaven, or dominating the entire world, attaining stream-entry is better.
passages.title: Dhammapada 178 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter of the World
passages.original: Pathabyā ekarajjena,  saggassa gamanena vā;  Sabbalokādhipaccena,  sotāpattiphalaṁ varaṁ.

passages.text: One whose victory does not diminish, whose victory cannot be removed by anyone in the world, the domain of that Awakened One is infinite - No one can lead that one astray.
passages.title: Dhammapada 179 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati,  Jitaṁ yassa noyāti koci loke;  Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ,  Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.

passages.text: One who is not entangled or stuck, in whom no craving can be found, the domain of that Awakened One is infinite - No one can lead that one astray.
passages.title: Dhammapada 180 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Yassa jālinī visattikā,  Taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave;  Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ,  Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.

passages.text: They are steadfast, committed to Jhāna, appreciate the peacefulness of renunciation, and are envied even by the angels - those who are mindful and fully Awakened.
passages.title: Dhammapada 181 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā,  nekkhammūpasame ratā;  Devāpi tesaṁ pihayanti,  sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.

passages.text: It is hard to become a human, it is hard to live a mortal life, it is hard to hear the true Dhamma, it is hard to encounter an Awakened One.
passages.title: Dhammapada 182 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho,  kicchaṁ maccāna jīvitaṁ;  Kicchaṁ saddhammassavanaṁ,  kiccho buddhānamuppādo.

passages.text: Not doing anything evil, commitment to the wholesome, and cleansing one's own mind - this is the teaching of the Awakened Ones.
passages.title: Dhammapada 183 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ,  kusalassa upasampadā;  Sacittapariyodapanaṁ,  etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.

passages.text: Endurance is the highest austerity, Nibbāna is the highest, according to those who are Awakened. A renunciant does not harm others, a contemplative does not oppress others.
passages.title: Dhammapada 184 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Khantī paramaṁ tapo titikkhā,  Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ vadanti buddhā;  Na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī,  Na samaṇo hoti paraṁ viheṭhayanto.

passages.text: Not insulting, not harming, self-restraint in accordance with the Pātimokkha, Knowing the right amount when eating, sitting and sleeping in a secluded place, and commitment to improving the mind - this is the teaching of the Awakened Ones.
passages.title: Dhammapada 185 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Anūpavādo anūpaghāto,  Pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro;  Mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ,  Pantañca sayanāsanaṁ;  Adhicitte ca āyogo,  Etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.

passages.text: Not even with a rain of money can one be sated when it comes to sensuality. There is little gratification in sensuality, it is unsatisfying; this is what the wise understand.
passages.title: Dhammapada 186 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Na kahāpaṇavassena,  titti kāmesu vijjati;  Appassādā dukhā kāmā,  iti viññāya paṇḍito.

passages.text: Even in heavenly sensuality one cannot find satisfaction. But there is satisfaction in the elimination of craving for a disciple of the Fully Awakened One.
passages.title: Dhammapada 187 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Api dibbesu kāmesu,  ratiṁ so nādhigacchati;  Taṇhakkhayarato hoti,  sammāsambuddhasāvako.

passages.text: They go to many places for refuge - mountains, groves, forest shrines - people who are struck by fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 188 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti,  pabbatāni vanāni ca;  Ārāmarukkhacetyāni,  manussā bhayatajjitā.

passages.text: But that is not a secure refuge, that is not the ultimate refuge; that is not a refuge which brings freedom from all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 189 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Netaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ,  netaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ;  Netaṁ saraṇamāgamma,  sabbadukkhā pamuccati.

passages.text: But one who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha, and who sees the Four Noble Truths with correct wisdom -
passages.title: Dhammapada 190 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Yo ca buddhañca dhammañca,  saṅghañca saraṇaṁ gato;  Cattāri ariyasaccāni,  sammappaññāya passati.

passages.text: suffering, the origin of suffering, the transcending of suffering, and the Noble Eightfold Path which leads to the pacification of suffering -
passages.title: Dhammapada 191 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ,  dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ;  Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,  dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.

passages.text: this is a secure refuge, this is the ultimate refuge. This is the refuge which brings freedom from all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 192 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Etaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ,  etaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ;  Etaṁ saraṇamāgamma,  sabbadukkhā pamuccati.

passages.text: It is hard to find a high-quality person; they are not born everywhere. Wherever a steadfast person is born, their family grows in happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 193 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Dullabho purisājañño,  na so sabbattha jāyati;  Yattha so jāyati dhīro,  taṁ kulaṁ sukhamedhati.

passages.text: Happy is the arising of Awakened Ones, happy is the teaching of the true Dhamma, happy is the harmony of the Sangha, happy is the austerity of those on the same Path.
passages.title: Dhammapada 194 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Sukho buddhānamuppādo,  sukhā saddhammadesanā;  Sukhā saṅghassa sāmaggī,  samaggānaṁ tapo sukho.

passages.text: One who honors those worthy of honor - Awakened Ones or their disciples, those who have transcended complication and gone beyond sorrow and grief,
passages.title: Dhammapada 195 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Pūjārahe pūjayato,  buddhe yadi va sāvake;  Papañcasamatikkante,  tiṇṇasokapariddave.

passages.text: who have reached Nibbāna, and are fearless - it is not possible to calculate the merit of one who honors such beings.
passages.title: Dhammapada 196 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Buddha
passages.original: Te tādise pūjayato,  nibbute akutobhaye;  Na sakkā puññaṁ saṅkhātuṁ,  imettamapi kenaci.

passages.text: Oh so happily we live, non-hostile amidst the hostile. Amidst hostile people we live without hostility.
passages.title: Dhammapada 197 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  verinesu averino;  Verinesu manussesu,  viharāma averino.

passages.text: Oh so happily we live, unafflicted amidst the afflicted. Amidst afflicted people we live without affliction.
passages.title: Dhammapada 198 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  āturesu anāturā;  Āturesu manussesu,  viharāma anāturā.

passages.text: Oh so happily we live, unpreoccupied amidst the preoccupied. Amidst preoccupied people we live without preoccupation.
passages.title: Dhammapada 199 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  ussukesu anussukā;  Ussukesu manussesu,  viharāma anussukā.

passages.text: Oh so happily we live, we who have nothing. We will feed on bliss, like the radiant angels.
passages.title: Dhammapada 200 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  yesaṁ no natthi kiñcanaṁ;  Pītibhakkhā bhavissāma,  devā ābhassarā yathā.

passages.text: Victory produces hostility; the defeated sleep uncomfortably. The peaceful sleep happily, having relinquished both victory and defeat.
passages.title: Dhammapada 201 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Jayaṁ veraṁ pasavati,  dukkhaṁ seti parājito;  Upasanto sukhaṁ seti,  hitvā jayaparājayaṁ.

passages.text: There is no fire as strong as passion, no distress as strong as aversion, no suffering as strong as the components of being, no happiness greater than peace
passages.title: Dhammapada 202 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Natthi rāgasamo aggi,  Natthi dosasamo kali;  Natthi khandhasamā dukkhā,  Natthi santiparaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Hunger is the highest affliction, conditions are the highest suffering; for one who truly knows this, Nibbāna is the highest happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 203 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Jighacchāparamā rogā,  saṅkhāraparamā dukhā;  Etaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ,  nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Freedom from illness is the highest acquisition, contentment is the highest wealth, trust is the highest kin, Nibbāna is the highest happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 204 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Ārogyaparamā lābhā,  Santuṭṭhiparamaṁ dhanaṁ;  Vissāsaparamā ñāti,  Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Having tasted the flavor of seclusion and the flavor of peace, free from anguish, flawless, one tastes the bliss of the Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 205 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Pavivekarasaṁ pitvā,  rasaṁ upasamassa ca;  Niddaro hoti nippāpo,  dhammapītirasaṁ pivaṁ.

passages.text: It is good to see the Noble Ones, living with them is always pleasant. One who does not see fools will always be happy.
passages.title: Dhammapada 206 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Sāhu dassanamariyānaṁ,  sannivāso sadā sukho;  Adassanena bālānaṁ,  niccameva sukhī siyā.

passages.text: Those who go with fools will sorrow for a long time. Living with fools is painful, like being with an enemy all the time. But living with the wise is pleasant, like being together with one's relatives.
passages.title: Dhammapada 207 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Bālasaṅgatacārī hi,  dīghamaddhāna socati;  Dukkho bālehi saṁvāso,  amitteneva sabbadā;  Dhīro ca sukhasaṁvāso,  ñātīnaṁva samāgamo.

passages.text: Therefore, follow one who is steadfast, wise, and educated, a good person who is patient, religious, noble, and astute, follow that person, as the moon follows the path of the stars.
passages.title: Dhammapada 208 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Happiness
passages.original: Tasmā hi— Dhīrañca paññañca bahussutañca,  Dhorayhasīlaṁ vatavantamariyaṁ;  Taṁ tādisaṁ sappurisaṁ sumedhaṁ,  Bhajetha nakkhattapathaṁva candimā.

passages.text: One who is dedicated to that which is not worthy of dedication, and who is not dedicated to that which is worthy of dedication, has dropped the goal and grabbed their preferences - yet envies those who are intent upon self-development.
passages.title: Dhammapada 209 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Ayoge yuñjamattānaṁ,  yogasmiñca ayojayaṁ;  Atthaṁ hitvā piyaggāhī,  pihetattānuyoginaṁ.

passages.text: Don’t get caught up in what you prefer or in what you do not prefer. Not seeing what you prefer is hard to bear and so is seeing what you do not prefer.
passages.title: Dhammapada 210 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Mā piyehi samāgañchi,  appiyehi kudācanaṁ;  Piyānaṁ adassanaṁ dukkhaṁ,  appiyānañca dassanaṁ.

passages.text: Therefore don’t form any preference; loss of what one prefers is painful. One who has no attachments has no preferences.
passages.title: Dhammapada 211 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Tasmā piyaṁ na kayirātha,  piyāpāyo hi pāpako;  Ganthā tesaṁ na vijjanti,  yesaṁ natthi piyāppiyaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow is born from preference, fear is born from preference; one who is free from preference has no sorrow and no fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 212 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Piyato jāyatī soko,  piyato jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Piyato vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow is born from affection, fear is born from affection; one who is free from affection has no sorrow and no fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 213 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Pemato jāyatī soko,  pemato jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Pemato vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow is born from partiality, fear is born from partiality; one who is free from partiality has no sorrow and no fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 214 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Ratiyā jāyatī soko,  ratiyā jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Ratiyā vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow is born from sensuality, fear is born from sensuality; one who is free from sensuality has no sorrow and no fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 215 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Kāmato jāyatī soko,  kāmato jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Kāmato vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow is born from craving, fear is born from craving; one who is free from craving has no sorrow and no fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 216 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Taṇhāya jāyatī soko,  taṇhāya jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Taṇhāya vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: One who has perfect morality and wisdom, who is established in the Dhamma and understands truth, and who works on themself - this is the kind of person that the populace prefers.
passages.title: Dhammapada 217 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Sīladassanasampannaṁ,  dhammaṭṭhaṁ saccavedinaṁ;  Attano kamma kubbānaṁ,  taṁ jano kurute piyaṁ.

passages.text: Interested in the inexpressible, with an expanded mind, and not bound by sensuality - such a one is said be going upstream.
passages.title: Dhammapada 218 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Chandajāto anakkhāte,  Manasā ca phuṭo siyā;  Kāmesu ca appaṭibaddhacitto,  Uddhaṁsototi vuccati.

passages.text: When a person who has been away for a long time arrives safely from afar, their relatives, friends, and loved ones delight in that arrival.
passages.title: Dhammapada 219 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Cirappavāsiṁ purisaṁ,  dūrato sotthimāgataṁ;  Ñātimittā suhajjā ca,  abhinandanti āgataṁ.

passages.text: In the same way, when one who has made merit goes from this world to the next, they are received by their merit like the arrival of a beloved relative.
passages.title: Dhammapada 220 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Preference Chapter
passages.original: Tatheva katapuññampi,  asmā lokā paraṁ gataṁ;  Puññāni paṭigaṇhanti,  piyaṁ ñātīva āgataṁ.

passages.text: Non-negligence is the path of the Deathless, negligence is the path of death. Those who are not negligent never die, those who are negligent are like the dead.
passages.title: Dhammapada 21 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Appamādo amatapadaṁ,  pamādo maccuno padaṁ;  Appamattā na mīyanti,  ye pamattā yathā matā.

passages.text: This is what the wise distinctly know about non-negligence. They rejoice in non-negligence, enjoying the territory of the noble ones.
passages.title: Dhammapada 22 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Evaṁ visesato ñatvā,  appamādamhi paṇḍitā;  Appamāde pamodanti,  ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.

passages.text: Those who meditate continuously, who always persevere, Steadfast, they touch Nibbāna— the unsurpassable safety.
passages.title: Dhammapada 23 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Te jhāyino sātatikā,  niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā;  Phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṁ,  yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.

passages.text: Glory increases for those who are proactive and mindful, with pure and careful conduct, self-restrained, living the Dhamma, and not negligent.
passages.title: Dhammapada 24 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato,  Sucikammassa nisammakārino;  Saññatassa dhammajīvino,  Appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.

passages.text: By being proactive and not negligent, self-restrained and self-controlled, a wise person makes an island which no flood can submerge.
passages.title: Dhammapada 25 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Uṭṭhānenappamādena,  saṁyamena damena ca;  Dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī,  yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.

passages.text: Fools and idiots commit to negligence, whereas a wise person protects non-negligence as the greatest wealth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 26 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Pamādamanuyuñjanti,  bālā dummedhino janā;  Appamādañca medhāvī,  dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁva rakkhati.

passages.text: Do not commit to negligence or to involvement in sensuality; for one who meditates without negligence attains abundant bliss.
passages.title: Dhammapada 27 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha,  mā kāmaratisanthavaṁ;  Appamatto hi jhāyanto,  pappoti vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: When a wise person dispels negligence by practicing non-negligence, then having ascended in the palace of wisdom, sorrowless, they look at this sorrowful generation, as a wise person on a mountain looks down at the fools on the ground.
passages.title: Dhammapada 28 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Pamādaṁ appamādena,  yadā nudati paṇḍito;  Paññāpāsādamāruyha,  asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ;  Pabbataṭṭhova bhūmaṭṭhe,  dhīro bāle avekkhati.

passages.text: Not negligent amidst the negligent, wide awake amidst the sleeping— like a swift horse leaving behind a feeble one, the wise leave them behind and move on.
passages.title: Dhammapada 29 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Appamatto pamattesu,  suttesu bahujāgaro;  Abalassaṁva sīghasso,  hitvā yāti sumedhaso.

passages.text: By means of non-negligence Maghavā became the best of the angels; they praise non-negligence, whereas negligence is always criticized.
passages.title: Dhammapada 30 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Appamādena maghavā,  devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato;  Appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti,  pamādo garahito sadā.

passages.text: A monk who approves of non-negligence and sees the danger in negligence proceeds like a fire— burning up fetters, small and large.
passages.title: Dhammapada 31 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Appamādarato bhikkhu,  pamāde bhayadassi vā;  Saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ thūlaṁ,  ḍahaṁ aggīva gacchati.

passages.text: A monk who approves of non-negligence and sees the danger in negligence cannot decline and is close to Nibbāna.
passages.title: Dhammapada 32 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Non-Negligence
passages.original: Appamādarato bhikkhu,  pamāde bhayadassi vā;  Abhabbo parihānāya,  nibbānasseva santike.
