passages.text: Abandon anger, discard conceit, completely transcend the fetter; Not adhering to mind and body, possessing nothing, one does not fall into suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 221 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Kodhaṁ jahe vippajaheyya mānaṁ,  Saṁyojanaṁ sabbamatikkameyya;  Taṁ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṁ,  Akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.

passages.text: When anger arises, one who stops it like a runaway cart - That is the one I call a charioteer; other people just hold the reins.
passages.title: Dhammapada 222 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Yo ve uppatitaṁ kodhaṁ,  rathaṁ bhantaṁva vāraye;  Tamahaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi,  rasmiggāho itaro jano.

passages.text: By means of non-anger one defeats anger, by means of excellence one defeats non-excellence, by means of generosity one defeats stinginess, by means of truth one defeats lies.
passages.title: Dhammapada 223 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ,  asādhuṁ sādhunā jine;  Jine kadariyaṁ dānena,  saccenālikavādinaṁ.

passages.text: Speak the truth, do not get angry, and give - even just a little bit - when asked; by means of these three things you will enter the presence of the angels.
passages.title: Dhammapada 224 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Saccaṁ bhaṇe na kujjheyya,  dajjā appampi yācito;  Etehi tīhi ṭhānehi,  gacche devāna santike.

passages.text: Those sages who are harmless, who are always physically restrained, go to the undying state where they do not sorrow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 225 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Ahiṁsakā ye munayo,  niccaṁ kāyena saṁvutā;  Te yanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ,  yattha gantvā na socare.

passages.text: When one is always wakeful, training day and night, and intent upon Nibbāna, their defilements disappear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 226 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Sadā jāgaramānānaṁ,  ahorattānusikkhinaṁ;  Nibbānaṁ adhimuttānaṁ,  atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.

passages.text: This is an incomparably ancient truth, not just the way it is today: they criticize those who are silent, they criticize those who speak a lot, they criticize those who speak moderately; there is no one in the world who is not criticized.
passages.title: Dhammapada 227 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Porāṇametaṁ atula,  netaṁ ajjatanāmiva;  Nindanti tuṇhimāsīnaṁ,  nindanti bahubhāṇinaṁ;  Mitabhāṇimpi nindanti,  natthi loke anindito.

passages.text: It has not been, it will not be, and it is not now the case that anyone is exclusively criticized or exclusively praised.
passages.title: Dhammapada 228 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Na cāhu na ca bhavissati,  na cetarahi vijjati;  Ekantaṁ nindito poso,  ekantaṁ vā pasaṁsito.

passages.text: The discerning praise one who, when observed day after day, is known to have impeccable conduct, intelligence, wisdom, morality, and concentration.
passages.title: Dhammapada 229 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Yañce viññū pasaṁsanti,  anuvicca suve suve;  Acchiddavuttiṁ medhāviṁ,  paññāsīlasamāhitaṁ.

passages.text: Such a person is like a gold coin - who would be worthy to criticize them? Even the angels praise such a person; even Brahmā praises such a person.
passages.title: Dhammapada 230 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Nikkhaṁ jambonadasseva,  ko taṁ ninditumarahati;  Devāpi naṁ pasaṁsanti,  brahmunāpi pasaṁsito.

passages.text: Protect yourself from manifesting anger physically; practice physical self-restraint. Having relinquished physical misconduct, practice good conduct with the body.
passages.title: Dhammapada 231 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Kāyappakopaṁ rakkheyya,  kāyena saṁvuto siyā;  Kāyaduccaritaṁ hitvā,  kāyena sucaritaṁ care.

passages.text: Protect yourself from manifesting anger verbally; practice verbal self-restraint. Having relinquished verbal misconduct, practice good conduct with speech.
passages.title: Dhammapada 232 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Vacīpakopaṁ rakkheyya,  vācāya saṁvuto siyā;  Vacīduccaritaṁ hitvā,  vācāya sucaritaṁ care.

passages.text: Protect yourself from manifesting anger mentally; practice mental self-restraint. Having relinquished mental misconduct, practice good conduct with the mind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 233 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Manopakopaṁ rakkheyya,  manasā saṁvuto siyā;  Manoduccaritaṁ hitvā,  manasā sucaritaṁ care.

passages.text: The steadfast are self-restrained physically, verbally, and mentally; they are well-restrained in every way.
passages.title: Dhammapada 234 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Anger Chapter
passages.original: Kāyena saṁvutā dhīrā,  atho vācāya saṁvutā;  Manasā saṁvutā dhīrā,  te ve suparisaṁvutā.

passages.text: Now you are like a fallen leaf, and Death's minions are near. You stand at the starting point of a struggle, and no provisions can be found for you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 235 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Paṇḍupalāsova dānisi,  Yamapurisāpi ca te upaṭṭhitā;  Uyyogamukhe ca tiṭṭhasi,  Pātheyyampi ca te na vijjati.

passages.text: Make an island for yourself, quickly try to become wise; one who has no contaminants and no flaws will reach the divine state of the noble ones.
passages.title: Dhammapada 236 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: So karohi dīpamattano,  Khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava;  Niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo,  Dibbaṁ ariyabhūmiṁ upehisi.

passages.text: Now you are close to departing; you are in the presence of Death. You have nowhere to dwell here, and no provisions can be found for you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 237 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Upanītavayo ca dānisi,  Sampayātosi yamassa santikaṁ;  Vāso te natthi antarā,  Pātheyyampi ca te na vijjati.

passages.text: Make an island for yourself, quickly try to become wise; one who has no contaminants and no flaws does not come again to birth and decrepitude.
passages.title: Dhammapada 238 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: So karohi dīpamattano,  Khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava;  Niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo,  Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.

passages.text: Progressively, bit by bit, moment after moment, like a smith purifying silver, the wise remove their contaminants.
passages.title: Dhammapada 239 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Anupubbena medhāvī,  thokaṁ thokaṁ khaṇe khaṇe;  Kammāro rajatasseva,  niddhame malamattano.

passages.text: When rust appears it eats away the metal that produced it; in the same way, a sanctimonious person is led to a bad destination by their own actions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 240 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Ayasāva malaṁ samuṭṭhitaṁ,  Tatuṭṭhāya tameva khādati;  Evaṁ atidhonacārinaṁ,  Sāni kammāni nayanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: Non-repetition contaminates mantras, non-upkeep contaminates a house, laziness contaminates beauty, negligence contaminates security.
passages.title: Dhammapada 241 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Asajjhāyamalā mantā,  anuṭṭhānamalā gharā;  Malaṁ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṁ,  pamādo rakkhato malaṁ.

passages.text: Misconduct contaminates a woman, stinginess contaminates a donor, evil choices contaminate both this life and the next.
passages.title: Dhammapada 242 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Malitthiyā duccaritaṁ,  maccheraṁ dadato malaṁ;  Malā ve pāpakā dhammā,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

passages.text: There is a contaminant that is even worse than that: ignorance, the paramount contaminant. Abandon this contaminant and be free of contaminants, monks!
passages.title: Dhammapada 243 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Tato malā malataraṁ,  avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ;  Etaṁ malaṁ pahantvāna,  nimmalā hotha bhikkhavo.

passages.text: It is easy to lose one's conscience, to act like an impudent and offensive crow, obtrusive and inconsiderate, living a defiled life.
passages.title: Dhammapada 244 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Sujīvaṁ ahirikena,  kākasūrena dhaṁsinā;  Pakkhandinā pagabbhena,  saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ.

passages.text: It is not easy to maintain one's conscience, always seeking to be impeccable, one who is diligent and considerate, insightful and living a life of purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 245 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Hirīmatā ca dujjīvaṁ,  niccaṁ sucigavesinā;  Alīnenāppagabbhena,  suddhājīvena passatā.

passages.text: One who kills, lies, steals, commits adultery,
passages.title: Dhammapada 246 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Yo pāṇamatipāteti,  musāvādañca bhāsati;  Loke adinnamādiyati,  paradārañca gacchati.

passages.text: and drinks alcohol - a person who engages in such activities right here in this world destroys their own foundation.
passages.title: Dhammapada 247 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Surāmerayapānañca,  yo naro anuyuñjati;  Idheva meso lokasmiṁ,  mūlaṁ khaṇati attano.

passages.text: Therefore, you should know that lack of restraint is evil; do not let greed contrary to Dhamma afflict you with long-lasting suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 248 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Evaṁ bho purisa jānāhi,  pāpadhammā asaññatā;  Mā taṁ lobho adhammo ca,  ciraṁ dukkhāya randhayuṁ.

passages.text: People give because it brings faith and joy. One who is disturbed when food and drink are given to others does not gain concentration by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 249 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Dadāti ve yathāsaddhaṁ,  yathāpasādanaṁ jano;  Tattha yo ca maṅku bhavati,  paresaṁ pānabhojane;  Na so divā vā rattiṁ vā,  samādhimadhigacchati.

passages.text: One who has shredded, uprooted, and destroyed that attitude gains concentration by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 250 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ,  mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ;  Sa ve divā vā rattiṁ vā,  samādhimadhigacchati.

passages.text: There is no fire as strong as passion, no grasp as strong as aversion, no trap as strong as delusion, no river as strong as craving.
passages.title: Dhammapada 251 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Natthi rāgasamo aggi,  natthi dosasamo gaho;  Natthi mohasamaṁ jālaṁ,  natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.

passages.text: It is easy to see the faults of others, and hard to see our own. When we frequently expose the faults of others but conceal our own, we are like a fraud cheating at dice.
passages.title: Dhammapada 252 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Sudassaṁ vajjamaññesaṁ,  attano pana duddasaṁ;  Paresaṁ hi so vajjāni,  opunāti yathā bhusaṁ;  Attano pana chādeti,  kaliṁva kitavā saṭho.

passages.text: When one looks at the faults of others and is always looking to criticize, one's defilements grow and one is far the elimination of defilements.
passages.title: Dhammapada 253 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Paravajjānupassissa,  niccaṁ ujjhānasaññino;  Āsavā tassa vaḍḍhanti,  ārā so āsavakkhayā.

passages.text: There is no path in the sky, there is no contemplative elsewhere. People delight in complication, whereas a Truth-Finder is free of complication.
passages.title: Dhammapada 254 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Ākāseva padaṁ natthi,  samaṇo natthi bāhire;  Papañcābhiratā pajā,  nippapañcā tathāgatā.

passages.text: There is no path in the sky, there is no contemplative elsewhere. There is nothing that is eternal, and no agitation in Buddhas.
passages.title: Dhammapada 255 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Contaminant Chapter
passages.original: Ākāseva padaṁ natthi,  samaṇo natthi bāhire;  Saṅkhārā sassatā natthi,  natthi buddhānamiñjitaṁ.

passages.text: One is not established in Dhamma if one seeks benefit using violence; a wise person does not wish to have both benefit and detriment.
passages.title: Dhammapada 256 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na tena hoti dhammaṭṭho,  yenatthaṁ sāhasā naye;  Yo ca atthaṁ anatthañca,  ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.

passages.text: One who guides others nonviolently, peacefully, in accordance with Dhamma, such a wise person is a guardian of the Dhamma and is said to be established in Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 257 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Asāhasena dhammena,  samena nayatī pare;  Dhammassa gutto medhāvī,  “dhammaṭṭho”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: One is not wise just because one talks a lot. One who is safe, non-hostile, harmless and fearless is said to be wise.
passages.title: Dhammapada 258 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na tena paṇḍito hoti,  yāvatā bahu bhāsati;  Khemī averī abhayo,  “paṇḍito”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: One is not an upholder of the Dhamma just because one talks a lot. Even if one has learned little but personally sees the Dhamma, then one is an upholder of the Dhamma, one who does not neglect the Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 259 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na tāvatā dhammadharo,  yāvatā bahu bhāsati;  Yo ca appampi sutvāna,  dhammaṁ kāyena passati;  Sa ve dhammadharo hoti,  yo dhammaṁ nappamajjati.

passages.text: One is not an elder just because one has grey hairs on one's head. One is who is decrepit and feeble is said to be an old fool.
passages.title: Dhammapada 260 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na tena thero so hoti,  yenassa palitaṁ siro;  Paripakko vayo tassa,  “moghajiṇṇo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: But one who is truthful, in accordance with the Dhamma, harmless, self-restrained, trained, steadfast, and free of all contaminants is said to be an elder.
passages.title: Dhammapada 261 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca,  ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo;  Sa ve vantamalo dhīro,  “thero” iti pavuccati.

passages.text: Not by the quality of their conversation or the beauty of their appearance is a person considered excellent, if they are envious, stingy, and deceitful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 262 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na vākkaraṇamattena,  vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā;  Sādhurūpo naro hoti,  issukī maccharī saṭho.

passages.text: One who has shredded, uprooted, and destroyed those qualities, a wise person who has expelled their defects, is said to be excellent.
passages.title: Dhammapada 263 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ,  mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ;  Sa vantadoso medhāvī,  “sādhurūpo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: One is not a contemplative just because one has a shaven head. If one has no religious practices, tells lies, and is full of desire and greed, how can they be a contemplative?
passages.title: Dhammapada 264 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo,  abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ;  Icchālobhasamāpanno,  samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati.

passages.text: One who tranquilizes all that is evil, whether minor or major, one who has tranquilized all that is evil is said to be a contemplative.
passages.title: Dhammapada 265 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Yo ca sameti pāpāni,  aṇuṁthūlāni sabbaso;  Samitattā hi pāpānaṁ,  “samaṇo”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: One is not a monk just because one receives almsfood from others. One who takes up a flawed doctrine is not a monk.
passages.title: Dhammapada 266 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na tena bhikkhu so hoti,  yāvatā bhikkhate pare;  Vissaṁ dhammaṁ samādāya,  bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.

passages.text: One who has discarded both merit and evil, lives a spiritual life, and wanders in the world with careful consideration is said to be a monk.
passages.title: Dhammapada 267 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Yodha puññañca pāpañca,  bāhetvā brahmacariyavā;  Saṅkhāya loke carati,  sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.

passages.text: One is not a sage if they act like one yet are confused and ignorant. A wise person who carefully weighs their options, chooses the best,
passages.title: Dhammapada 268 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na monena munī hoti,  mūḷharūpo aviddasu;  Yo ca tulaṁva paggayha,  varamādāya paṇḍito.

passages.text: and completely avoids evil is a sage; because of this one is a sage. One who evaluates both of these in the world is said to be a sage.
passages.title: Dhammapada 269 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Pāpāni parivajjeti,  sa munī tena so muni;  Yo munāti ubho loke,  “muni” tena pavuccati.

passages.text: One is not noble if one harms living beings. One who does not harm any living being is said to be noble.
passages.title: Dhammapada 270 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na tena ariyo hoti,  yena pāṇāni hiṁsati;  Ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ,  “ariyo”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: Not just by morality or by spiritual practices or by learning a lot or by gaining concentration or by sleeping in seclusion
passages.title: Dhammapada 271 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Na sīlabbatamattena,  bāhusaccena vā pana;  Atha vā samādhilābhena,  vivittasayanena vā.

passages.text: or by experiencing the happiness of renunciation or by associating with uncommon people should a monk be satisfied as long as one’s defilements have not been eliminated.
passages.title: Dhammapada 272 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The “Established in Dhamma” Chapter
passages.original: Phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṁ,  aputhujjanasevitaṁ;  Bhikkhu vissāsamāpādi,  appatto āsavakkhayaṁ.

passages.text: The best of paths is the Eightfold; of truths, the one in four steps. The best of qualities is dispassion; of bipeds, the one who sees.
passages.title: Dhammapada 273 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho,  saccānaṁ caturo padā;  Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ,  dvipadānañca cakkhumā.

passages.text: This is the path - there is no other - for obtaining vision and purity. Therefore, follow this path which confuses Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 274 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Eseva maggo natthañño,  Dassanassa visuddhiyā;  Etañhi tumhe paṭipajjatha,  Mārassetaṁ pamohanaṁ.

passages.text: When you have followed this path you will end suffering. I have explained the path for you; by means of knowledge the sting is eased.
passages.title: Dhammapada 275 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Etañhi tumhe paṭipannā,  dukkhassantaṁ karissatha;  Akkhāto vo mayā maggo,  aññāya sallakantanaṁ.

passages.text: It is by you that the effort must be made; the Truth-Finders just explain. Those who have followed the path become free from the bonds of Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 276 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Tumhehi kiccamātappaṁ,  akkhātāro tathāgatā;  Paṭipannā pamokkhanti,  jhāyino mārabandhanā.

passages.text: Everything is impermanent - when one sees this with wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with suffering; this is the path to purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 277 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: “Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti,  yadā paññāya passati;  Atha nibbindati dukkhe,  esa maggo visuddhiyā.

passages.text: Everything is unsatisfying - when one sees this with wisdom one becomes disenchanted with suffering; this is the path to purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 278 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: “Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā”ti,  yadā paññāya passati;  Atha nibbindati dukkhe,  esa maggo visuddhiyā.

passages.text: Everything is impersonal - when one sees this with wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with suffering; this is the path to purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 279 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: “Sabbe dhammā anattā”ti,  yadā paññāya passati;  Atha nibbindati dukkhe,  esa maggo visuddhiyā.

passages.text: Not rising to the occasion when it is time to do so, young and strong, but indolent, aimless, and lazy, the indolent one does not find the path of wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 280 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Uṭṭhānakālamhi anuṭṭhahāno,  Yuvā balī ālasiyaṁ upeto;  Saṁsannasaṅkappamano kusīto,  Paññāya maggaṁ alaso na vindati.

passages.text: With speech controlled and mind well-restrained, and doing nothing harmful with the body, purify these three paths of karma and accomplish the path demonstrated by the seer.
passages.title: Dhammapada 281 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Vācānurakkhī manasā susaṁvuto,  Kāyena ca nākusalaṁ kayirā;  Ete tayo kammapathe visodhaye,  Ārādhaye maggamisippaveditaṁ.

passages.text: Commitment produces abundance, a lack of commitment completely eliminates it. Knowing these two paths which lead to existence and non-existence, one should settle oneself accordingly and cultivate abundance.
passages.title: Dhammapada 282 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri,  ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo;  Etaṁ dvedhāpathaṁ ñatvā,  bhavāya vibhavāya ca;  Tathāttānaṁ niveseyya,  yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Cut down the forest, not the tree; the forest produces danger. When you have cut down the forest and its undergrowth, you will have no forest, monks.
passages.title: Dhammapada 283 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Vanaṁ chindatha mā rukkhaṁ,  vanato jāyate bhayaṁ;  Chetvā vanañca vanathañca,  nibbanā hotha bhikkhavo.

passages.text: As long as the undergrowth has not been cut down, even if only a tiny amount is left, then whether one is a man or a woman one will be bound to it, like a calf sucking milk from its mother.
passages.title: Dhammapada 284 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Yāva hi vanatho na chijjati,  Aṇumattopi narassa nārisu;  Paṭibaddhamanova tāva so,  Vaccho khīrapakova mātari.

passages.text: Cut off self-cherishing, like plucking a lotus in autumn. Practice the peaceful path to Nibbāna as taught by the Heavenly One.
passages.title: Dhammapada 285 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Ucchinda sinehamattano,  Kumudaṁ sāradikaṁva pāṇinā;  Santimaggameva brūhaya,  Nibbānaṁ sugatena desitaṁ.

passages.text: “Here I will spend the rainy season, here the winter, here the summer.” This is how a fool thinks, not aware of the obstacle.
passages.title: Dhammapada 286 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Idha vassaṁ vasissāmi,  idha hemantagimhisu;  Iti bālo vicinteti,  antarāyaṁ na bujjhati.

passages.text: Intoxicated with children and cattle, a person with mind attached; like a great flood sweeping away a sleeping village, such a person is swept away by death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 287 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Taṁ puttapasusammattaṁ,  byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ;  Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova,  maccu ādāya gacchati.

passages.text: There is no safety in children, parents, or kin; when one is seized by the Ender, there is no safety in relatives.
passages.title: Dhammapada 288 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Na santi puttā tāṇāya,  na pitā nāpi bandhavā;  Antakenādhipannassa,  natthi ñātīsu tāṇatā.

passages.text: Having understood this issue, the wise person, moral and self-restrained, quickly purifies the path that leads to Nibbāna.
passages.title: Dhammapada 289 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Path Chapter
passages.original: Etamatthavasaṁ ñatvā,  paṇḍito sīlasaṁvuto;  Nibbānagamanaṁ maggaṁ,  khippameva visodhaye.

passages.text: If by relinquishing limited happiness one can see abundant happiness, then one who is wise relinquishes limited happiness and sees abundant happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 290 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Mattāsukhapariccāgā,  passe ce vipulaṁ sukhaṁ;  Caje mattāsukhaṁ dhīro,  sampassaṁ vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: By profiting from the suffering of others, one seeks happiness for oneself; one who is intimately involved in hostility is not free from hostility.
passages.title: Dhammapada 291 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Paradukkhūpadhānena,  attano sukhamicchati;  Verasaṁsaggasaṁsaṭṭho,  verā so na parimuccati.

passages.text: They reject what should be done and do what should not be done; arrogant and negligent, their defilements increase.
passages.title: Dhammapada 292 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Yañhi kiccaṁ apaviddhaṁ,  akiccaṁ pana karīyati;  Unnaḷānaṁ pamattānaṁ,  tesaṁ vaḍḍhanti āsavā.

passages.text: They have undertaken continuous mindfulness of the body, they do not do what should not be done, and they always do what should be done; mindful and aware, their defilements disappear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 293 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Yesañca susamāraddhā,  niccaṁ kāyagatā sati;  Akiccaṁ te na sevanti,  kicce sātaccakārino;  Satānaṁ sampajānānaṁ,  atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.

passages.text: Having slain mother and father, two royal kings, and a kingdom with its followers, the brahmin proceeds untroubled.
passages.title: Dhammapada 294 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā,  rājāno dve ca khattiye;  Raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā,  anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: Having slain mother and father, two scholar kings, and a tiger as well, the brahmin proceeds untroubled.
passages.title: Dhammapada 295 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā,  rājāno dve ca sotthiye;  Veyagghapañcamaṁ hantvā,  anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: They always wake up well, the disciples of Gotama who continuously recollect the Buddha by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 296 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ buddhagatā sati.

passages.text: They always wake up well, disciples of the Buddha who continuously recollect the Dhamma by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 297 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ dhammagatā sati.

passages.text: They always wake up well, the disciples of Gotama who continuously recollect the Saṅgha by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 298 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ saṅghagatā sati.

passages.text: They always wake up well, the disciples of Gotama who continuously practice mindfulness of the body by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 299 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ kāyagatā sati.

passages.text: They always wake up well, the disciples of Gotama who approve of harmlessness by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 300 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  ahiṁsāya rato mano.

passages.text: They always wake up well, the disciples of Gotama who approve of self-development by day and by night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 301 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  bhāvanāya rato mano.

passages.text: The renunciant life is difficult and hard to enjoy; the household life is difficult and hard to endure. Living with others is suffering, and travelers also undergo suffering. Therefore, just as one can choose to not travel, one can choose to not suffer.
passages.title: Dhammapada 302 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Duppabbajjaṁ durabhiramaṁ,  Durāvāsā gharā dukhā;  Dukkhosamānasaṁvāso,  Dukkhānupatitaddhagū;  Tasmā na caddhagū siyā,  Na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.

passages.text: One who has faith and morality, influence and wealth, is honored wherever they are.
passages.title: Dhammapada 303 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Saddho sīlena sampanno,  yasobhogasamappito;  Yaṁ yaṁ padesaṁ bhajati,  tattha tattheva pūjito.

passages.text: Those who are good are visible from afar, like a Himalayan mountain; but those who are not good cannot be seen, like arrows loosed at night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 304 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Dūre santo pakāsenti,  himavantova pabbato;  Asantettha na dissanti,  rattiṁ khittā yathā sarā.

passages.text: Sitting alone, sleeping alone, going alone, never lazy; training oneself alone, one can enjoy the forest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 305 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Scattered Chapter
passages.original: Ekāsanaṁ ekaseyyaṁ,  eko caramatandito;  Eko damayamattānaṁ,  vanante ramito siyā.

passages.text: Those who proclaim what never happened go to hell, as well as those who do something then say they did not. After death, both are the same; people whose afterlife was determined by lowly actions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 306 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Abhūtavādī nirayaṁ upeti,  Yo vāpi katvā na karomi cāha;  Ubhopi te pecca samā bhavanti,  Nihīnakammā manujā parattha.

passages.text: Many who wear ochre on their neck are evil and unrestrained. Because of their evil actions they are reborn in hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 307 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo,  pāpadhammā asaññatā;  Pāpā pāpehi kammehi,  nirayaṁ te upapajjare.

passages.text: It is better to eat a red-hot iron ball, glowing like fire, than for an immoral, unrestrained person to eat the nation’s almsfood.
passages.title: Dhammapada 308 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto,  tatto aggisikhūpamo;  Yañce bhuñjeyya dussīlo,  raṭṭhapiṇḍamasaññato.

passages.text: Four things happen to a negligent person who commits adultery: bad karma, insomnia, criticism, and rebirth in hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 309 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto,  Āpajjati paradārūpasevī;  Apuññalābhaṁ na nikāmaseyyaṁ,  Nindaṁ tatīyaṁ nirayaṁ catutthaṁ.

passages.text: One acquires bad karma and the destiny of evil people, and only the minute pleasure of a frightened man with a frightened woman; and then the king enacts a severe punishment. Therefore, one should not commit adultery.
passages.title: Dhammapada 310 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Apuññalābho ca gatī ca pāpikā,  Bhītassa bhītāya ratī ca thokikā;  Rājā ca daṇḍaṁ garukaṁ paṇeti,  Tasmā naro paradāraṁ na seve.

passages.text: Just as a blade, when poorly held, cuts the hand that holds it, a contemplative life that is held incorrectly draws one closer to hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 311 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Kuso yathā duggahito,  hatthamevānukantati;  Sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ,  nirayāyupakaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Lax behavior, defiled practice, a suspicious spiritual life - this does not bring great benefit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 312 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ,  saṅkiliṭṭhañca yaṁ vataṁ;  Saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ,  na taṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: If one will do what one should do, then one should make a solid effort, because a lax renunciant scatters more dust.
passages.title: Dhammapada 313 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṁ,  daḷhamenaṁ parakkame;  Sithilo hi paribbājo,  bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.

passages.text: It is better when misconduct is not done; misconduct torments afterwards. It is better when good conduct is done; after doing so, one is not tormented.
passages.title: Dhammapada 314 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Akataṁ dukkaṭaṁ seyyo,  pacchā tappati dukkaṭaṁ;  Katañca sukataṁ seyyo,  yaṁ katvā nānutappati.

passages.text: As a border city is guarded inside and out, in the same way guard yourself; let not a moment slip past you. When the moment is past they sorrow, those who arrived in hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 315 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Nagaraṁ yathā paccantaṁ,  guttaṁ santarabāhiraṁ;  Evaṁ gopetha attānaṁ,  khaṇo vo mā upaccagā;  Khaṇātītā hi socanti,  nirayamhi samappitā.

passages.text: They are ashamed when they should not be ashamed, they are not ashamed when they should be ashamed; taking up wrong view, beings go to a bad destination.
passages.title: Dhammapada 316 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Alajjitāye lajjanti,  lajjitāye na lajjare;  Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: They see danger where there is no danger, they see no danger where there is danger; taking up wrong view, beings go to a bad destination.
passages.title: Dhammapada 317 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Abhaye bhayadassino,  bhaye cābhayadassino;  Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: They think the blameless is blameworthy, and see the blameworthy as blameless; taking up wrong view, beings go to a bad destination.
passages.title: Dhammapada 318 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Avajje vajjamatino,  vajje cāvajjadassino;  Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: Knowing the blameworthy as blameworthy and the blameless as blameless, taking up right view, beings go to a good destination.
passages.title: Dhammapada 319 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Hell Chapter
passages.original: Vajjañca vajjato ñatvā,  avajjañca avajjato;  Sammādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.

passages.text: Like an elephant in battle struck by an arrow from a bow, I will endure criticism from the immoral multitude.
passages.title: Dhammapada 320 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Ahaṁ nāgova saṅgāme,  cāpato patitaṁ saraṁ;  Ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ,  dussīlo hi bahujjano.

passages.text: One who is trained can be led through a crowd, one who is trained can be mounted by a king; a trained person is the best among humans, one who endures criticism.
passages.title: Dhammapada 321 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Dantaṁ nayanti samitiṁ,  dantaṁ rājābhirūhati;  Danto seṭṭho manussesu,  yotivākyaṁ titikkhati.

passages.text: Excellent are trained mules, well-bred Sindhi horses, and enormous elephants; but more excellent that those is one who is self-trained.
passages.title: Dhammapada 322 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Varamassatarā dantā,  ājānīyā ca sindhavā;  Kuñjarā ca mahānāgā,  attadanto tato varaṁ.

passages.text: For it is not by means of those vehicles that one goes in the direction one has never gone; where one who is self-trained, well-trained, can go by means of that training.
passages.title: Dhammapada 323 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Na hi etehi yānehi,  gaccheyya agataṁ disaṁ;  Yathāttanā sudantena,  danto dantena gacchati.

passages.text: The elephant named Dhanapāla is bitter about being separated, and is hard to restrain; captive, he does not eat, as he misses the elephant forest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 324 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Dhanapālo nāma kuñjaro,  Kaṭukabhedano dunnivārayo;  Baddho kabaḷaṁ na bhuñjati,  Sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.

passages.text: Lethargic and gluttonous, languid, lazing about, like an oversized pig that has taken the bait, the fool arrives again and again in the womb.
passages.title: Dhammapada 325 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca,  Niddāyitā samparivattasāyī;  Mahāvarāhova nivāpapuṭṭho,  Punappunaṁ gabbhamupeti mando.

passages.text: In the past this mind would wander, going wherever it wished, wherever it desired, wherever it found pleasure. Today I will subdue it with a wise understanding of causality, like an elephant-trainer subduing a rampaging elephant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 326 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Idaṁ pure cittamacāri cārikaṁ,  Yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ;  Tadajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso,  Hatthippabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.

passages.text: Approve of non-negligence, and guard your own mind. Lift yourself up from the harmful path, like an elephant lifting itself up from the mud.
passages.title: Dhammapada 327 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Appamādaratā hotha,  sacittamanurakkhatha;  Duggā uddharathattānaṁ,  paṅke sannova kuñjaro.

passages.text: If you can get a prudent companion to travel with, a steadfast person who lives an excellent life, then leave behind all your problems and go with them, satisfied and mindful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 328 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ,  Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ;  Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni,  Careyya tenattamano satīmā.

passages.text: If you can not get a prudent companion to travel with, a steadfast person who lives an excellent life, then like a king leaving behind a conquered realm, go alone, like an elephant in its wilderness habitat.
passages.title: Dhammapada 329 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ,  Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ;  Rājāva raṭṭhaṁ vijitaṁ pahāya,  Eko care mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.

passages.text: It is best to go alone; there is no companionship with a fool. One who lives alone and does nothing harmful will be at ease, like an elephant in its wilderness habitat.
passages.title: Dhammapada 330 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Ekassa caritaṁ seyyo,  Natthi bāle sahāyatā;  Eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā,  Appossukko mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.

passages.text: It is pleasant to have companions when the need arises, it is pleasant to be content with whatever comes, it is pleasant to have merit when life comes to an end, it is pleasant to leave behind all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 331 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā,  Tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena;  Puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi,  Sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahānaṁ.

passages.text: It is pleasant to be a mother in this world, it is pleasant to be a father; it is pleasant to be a contemplative in this world, it is pleasant to be spiritual.
passages.title: Dhammapada 332 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Sukhā matteyyatā loke,  atho petteyyatā sukhā;  Sukhā sāmaññatā loke,  atho brahmaññatā sukhā.

passages.text: It is pleasant to have virtue that lasts into old age, it is pleasant to have established faith, it is pleasant to have attained wisdom, it is pleasant to do no evil.
passages.title: Dhammapada 333 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Elephant Chapter
passages.original: Sukhaṁ yāva jarā sīlaṁ,  sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā;  Sukho paññāya paṭilābho,  pāpānaṁ akaraṇaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Unstable and unsteady is the mind, difficult to protect and restrain. The wise straighten it, like a fletcher straightens an arrow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 33 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ,  dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ;  Ujuṁ karoti medhāvī,  usukārova tejanaṁ.

passages.text: Like a fish pulled from its home and thrown on dry land, the mind thrashes about, struggling to escape the realm of Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 34 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Vārijova thale khitto,  okamokataubbhato;  Pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ,  māradheyyaṁ pahātave.

passages.text: The mind is fast-moving and hard to subdue, landing wherever it wishes; it is good to train it— a trained mind brings happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 35 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Dunniggahassa lahuno,  yatthakāmanipātino;  Cittassa damatho sādhu,  cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.

passages.text: The mind is very subtle and hard to see, landing wherever it wishes; the wise protect it— a guarded mind brings happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 36 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ,  yatthakāmanipātinaṁ;  Cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī,  cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.

passages.text: The mind travels far, wanders alone, incorporeal, self-sheltered; those who restrain it become free from the bonds of Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 37 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ,  asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ;  Ye cittaṁ saṁyamissanti,  mokkhanti mārabandhanā.

passages.text: For one whose mind is unsettled, who does not understand the true Dhamma, and whose clarity is disturbed, wisdom does not become complete.
passages.title: Dhammapada 38 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa,  saddhammaṁ avijānato;  Pariplavapasādassa,  paññā na paripūrati.

passages.text: One whose mind is free from influences, whose mind is unafflicted, who has abandoned both merit and evil, and is alert has no fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 39 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Anavassutacittassa,  ananvāhatacetaso;  Puññapāpapahīnassa,  natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Having understood that this body is like a clay pot, having fortified the mind like a city, combat Māra using wisdom as one's weapon, and protect the victory—you can be free of any abode.
passages.title: Dhammapada 40 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā,  Nagarūpamaṁ cittamidaṁ ṭhapetvā;  Yodhetha māraṁ paññāvudhena,  Jitañca rakkhe anivesano siyā.

passages.text: Before long, this body will lie on the ground discarded and devoid of consciousness like a useless log.
passages.title: Dhammapada 41 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo,  pathaviṁ adhisessati;  Chuddho apetaviññāṇo,  niratthaṁva kaliṅgaraṁ.

passages.text: Compared to what might be done by an enemy to an enemy or one hostile person to another, a wrongly directed mind can cause even more harm than that.
passages.title: Dhammapada 42 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Diso disaṁ yaṁ taṁ kayirā,  verī vā pana verinaṁ;  Micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ,  pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.

passages.text: Compared to what might be done by a mother or a father or any other relative, a rightly directed mind can bring even more benefit than that.
passages.title: Dhammapada 43 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Mind
passages.original: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā,  aññe vāpi ca ñātakā;  Sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ,  seyyaso naṁ tato kare.

passages.text: For a person who lives negligently, craving grows like vines; they drift from life to life, like a monkey in the forest wishing for fruit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 334 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Manujassa pamattacārino,  Taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya;  So plavatī hurā huraṁ,  Phalamicchaṁva vanasmi vānaro.

passages.text: When one is overcome by that which is despicable - craving, which keeps us stuck in the world - then sorrow grows in them, like weeds after rain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 335 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Yaṁ esā sahate jammī,  taṇhā loke visattikā;  Sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti,  abhivaṭṭhaṁva bīraṇaṁ.

passages.text: When one overcomes that which is despicable - craving, which is so hard to transcend in this world - then sorrow falls away from them, like drops of water from a lotus.
passages.title: Dhammapada 336 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Yo cetaṁ sahate jammiṁ,  taṇhaṁ loke duraccayaṁ;  Sokā tamhā papatanti,  udabinduva pokkharā.

passages.text: I wish the best to all of you that are gathered here - dig up the root of craving, as one seeks the root of a weed; do not let Māra subdue you again and again, like a stream does to reeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 337 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Taṁ vo vadāmi bhaddaṁ vo,  yāvantettha samāgatā;  Taṇhāya mūlaṁ khaṇatha,  usīratthova bīraṇaṁ;  Mā vo naḷaṁva sotova,  māro bhañji punappunaṁ.

passages.text: As long as its root is undisturbed and strong, a felled tree grows again. In the same way, as long as the tendency towards craving is not destroyed, it produces suffering again and again.
passages.title: Dhammapada 338 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Yathāpi mūle anupaddave daḷhe,  Chinnopi rukkho punareva rūhati;  Evampi taṇhānusaye anūhate,  Nibbattatī dukkhamidaṁ punappunaṁ.

passages.text: If the 36 streams are flowing strongly towards what one likes, then one is swept along by harmful views and attitudes based on passion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 339 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Yassa chattiṁsati sotā,  manāpasavanā bhusā;  Mahāvahanti duddiṭṭhiṁ,  saṅkappā rāganissitā.

passages.text: Streams flow everywhere, creepers appear and remain; having seen the birth of the creeper, cut its root with wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 340 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Savanti sabbadhi sotā,  latā uppajja tiṭṭhati;  Tañca disvā lataṁ jātaṁ,  mūlaṁ paññāya chindatha.

passages.text: Currents of infatuation and elation exist in people; those who are addicted to comfort, seeking pleasure, arrive at rebirth and decrepitude.
passages.title: Dhammapada 341 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Saritāni sinehitāni ca,  Somanassāni bhavanti jantuno;  Te sātasitā sukhesino,  Te ve jātijarūpagā narā.

passages.text: Pursued by craving, people thrash about like a trapped rabbit; bound by attachment and adherence, they come to suffering again and again for a long time.
passages.title: Dhammapada 342 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā,  Parisappanti sasova bandhito;  Saṁyojanasaṅgasattakā,  Dukkhamupenti punappunaṁ cirāya.

passages.text: Pursued by craving, people thrash about like a trapped rabbit; therefore, one should remove craving, wishing to be dispassionate.
passages.title: Dhammapada 343 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā,  Parisappanti sasova bandhito;  Tasmā tasiṇaṁ vinodaye,  Ākaṅkhanta virāgamattano.

passages.text: One who has left the forest yet is intent upon the forest, though free from the forest, runs back to the forest. Look at that person; although free, they run back to imprisonment.
passages.title: Dhammapada 344 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto,  Vanamutto vanameva dhāvati;  Taṁ puggalametha passatha,  Mutto bandhanameva dhāvati.

passages.text: The wise say that prisons made of iron, wood, and thatch are not as strong as obsession with jewelry, children, and spouses.
passages.title: Dhammapada 345 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Na taṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā,  Yadāyasaṁ dārujapabbajañca;  Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu,  Puttesu dāresu ca yā apekkhā.

passages.text: The wise say that this is a strong prison which oppresses the lax and is hard to escape from. They break free and become renunciants, leaving behind sensual pleasure without looking back.
passages.title: Dhammapada 346 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Etaṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā,  Ohārinaṁ sithilaṁ duppamuñcaṁ;  Etampi chetvāna paribbajanti,  Anapekkhino kāmasukhaṁ pahāya.

passages.text: Those who fall into the stream of passion are like a spider stuck in its own web. The wise break free and move on, leaving behind all suffering without looking back.
passages.title: Dhammapada 347 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ,  Sayaṅkataṁ makkaṭakova jālaṁ;  Etampi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā,  Anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṁ pahāya.

passages.text: Be free before, be free after, be free in the middle; transcend existence. With a mind liberated everywhere, do not return again to birth and decrepitude.
passages.title: Dhammapada 348 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Muñca pure muñca pacchato,  Majjhe muñca bhavassa pāragū;  Sabbattha vimuttamānaso,  Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.

passages.text: When one has disturbed thoughts, strong passion, and fixation on beauty, then craving grows ever greater and makes a strong prison.
passages.title: Dhammapada 349 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Vitakkamathitassa jantuno,  Tibbarāgassa subhānupassino;  Bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati,  Esa kho daḷhaṁ karoti bandhanaṁ.

passages.text: One who approves of tranquil thought, who has cultivated awareness of non-beauty and is always mindful, will put an end to that craving and break free of Māra’s prison.
passages.title: Dhammapada 350 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Vitakkūpasame ca yo rato,  Asubhaṁ bhāvayate sadā sato;  Esa kho byanti kāhiti,  Esa checchati mārabandhanaṁ.

passages.text: When one has reached the final destination, is fearless, free of craving, flawless, and has broken the thorn of existence, then they bear their last body.
passages.title: Dhammapada 351 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Niṭṭhaṅgato asantāsī,  vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo;  Acchindi bhavasallāni,  antimoyaṁ samussayo.

passages.text: When one is free of craving, not acquisitive, and is a master of words and phrases who knows the proper grouping and sequencing of sentences, then they are called a bearer of their last body, a great person of great wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 352 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Vītataṇho anādāno,  Niruttipadakovido;  Akkharānaṁ sannipātaṁ,  Jaññā pubbāparāni ca;  Sa ve “antimasārīro,  Mahāpañño mahāpuriso”ti vuccati.

passages.text: I have overcome all, I know all; amidst all things I am unsullied; I have relinquished everything and I am liberated through the elimination of craving - knowing this directly and personally, who could I indicate as my teacher?
passages.title: Dhammapada 353 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūhamasmi,  Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto;  Sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto,  Sayaṁ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṁ.

passages.text: The gift of Dhamma trumps all gifts, the taste of Dhamma trumps all tastes, the appreciation of Dhamma trumps all appreciation, the elimination of craving trumps all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 354 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Sabbadānaṁ dhammadānaṁ jināti,  Sabbarasaṁ dhammaraso jināti;  Sabbaratiṁ dhammarati jināti,  Taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti.

passages.text: Wealth destroys a fool who does not seek transcendence; a fool who craves wealth harms both self and others.
passages.title: Dhammapada 355 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Hananti bhogā dummedhaṁ,  no ca pāragavesino;  Bhogataṇhāya dummedho,  hanti aññeva attanaṁ.

passages.text: Grass is the defect of fields, passion is the defect of this generation; therefore a gift given to those free of passion is of great benefit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 356 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vītarāgesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Grass is the defect of fields, hatred is the defect of this generation; therefore a gift given to those free of hate is of great benefit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 357 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  dosadosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vītadosesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Grass is the defect of fields, delusion is the defect of this generation; therefore a gift given to those free of delusion is of great benefit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 358 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  mohadosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vītamohesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Grass is the defect of fields, craving is the defect of this generation; therefore a gift given to those free of craving is of great benefit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 359 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Craving Chapter
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  icchādosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vigaticchesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Excellent is restraint of the eye, excellent is restraint of the ear, excellent is restraint of the nose, excellent is restraint of the tongue,
passages.title: Dhammapada 360 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Cakkhunā saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu sotena saṁvaro;  Ghānena saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu jivhāya saṁvaro.

passages.text: excellent is restraint of the body, excellent is restraint of speech, excellent is restraint of the mind, excellent is restraint in every situation. A monk who is restrained in every situation is freed from all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 361 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Kāyena saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu vācāya saṁvaro;  Manasā saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu sabbattha saṁvaro;  Sabbattha saṁvuto bhikkhu,  sabbadukkhā pamuccati.

passages.text: Hand restrained, foot restrained, speech restrained, restrained to the utmost, appreciating introspection, concentrated, one who is content like this is called a monk.
passages.title: Dhammapada 362 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Hatthasaṁyato pādasaṁyato,  Vācāsaṁyato saṁyatuttamo;  Ajjhattarato samāhito,  Eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṁ.

passages.text: A monk who has a restrained mouth, who gives advice without arrogance, illuminates the meaning and the Dhamma, and their speech is like honey.
passages.title: Dhammapada 363 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Yo mukhasaṁyato bhikkhu,  mantabhāṇī anuddhato;  Atthaṁ dhammañca dīpeti,  madhuraṁ tassa bhāsitaṁ.

passages.text: Appreciating the Dhamma, approving of the Dhamma, investigating the Dhamma, remembering the Dhamma, a monk does not fall away from the true Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 364 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Dhammārāmo dhammarato,  dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ;  Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu,  saddhammā na parihāyati.

passages.text: One should not disdain what one has, nor envy what belongs to others; a monk who envies the belongings of others does not attain concentration.
passages.title: Dhammapada 365 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya,  nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care;  Aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu,  samādhiṁ nādhigacchati.

passages.text: Even if a monk has little, but does not disdain what he has, the angels praise him, the one who lives with purity and diligence.
passages.title: Dhammapada 366 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Appalābhopi ce bhikkhu,  salābhaṁ nātimaññati;  Taṁ ve devā pasaṁsanti,  suddhājīviṁ atanditaṁ.

passages.text: When there is nothing whatsoever in mind and body that one thinks of as “mine,” and one does not sorrow on account of the unpleasant, then one can be called a monk.
passages.title: Dhammapada 367 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ,  yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ;  Asatā ca na socati,  sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.

passages.text: A monk who maintains benevolence, and who has serene faith in the teaching of the Buddha, arrives at the peaceful path and the happiness of complete tranquility.
passages.title: Dhammapada 368 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu,  pasanno buddhasāsane;  Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ,  saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Bale out this boat, monk; when emptied, it moves easily. Having cut off passion and hatred, go from here to Nibbāna.
passages.title: Dhammapada 369 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Siñca bhikkhu imaṁ nāvaṁ,  sittā te lahumessati;  Chetvā rāgañca dosañca,  tato nibbānamehisi.

passages.text: When five are cut off and five are discarded, and another five are developed, then a monk who has gone beyond five attachments is said to have crossed the flood.
passages.title: Dhammapada 370 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Pañca chinde pañca jahe,  pañca cuttari bhāvaye;  Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu,  “oghatiṇṇo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: Meditate, monk, do not be negligent; do not let your mind swirl in sensuality. Do not negligently swallow a metal ball, complaining about suffering as you burn.
passages.title: Dhammapada 371 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Jhāya bhikkhu mā pamādo,  Mā te kāmaguṇe ramessu cittaṁ;  Mā lohaguḷaṁ gilī pamatto,  Mā kandi “dukkhamidan”ti dayhamāno.

passages.text: There is no Jhāna for one who has no wisdom; there is no wisdom for one who does not reach Jhāna. One who has both Jhāna and wisdom is close to Nibbāna.
passages.title: Dhammapada 372 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Natthi jhānaṁ apaññassa,  paññā natthi ajhāyato;  Yamhi jhānañca paññā ca,  sa ve nibbānasantike.

passages.text: In an empty hut, a monk with a peaceful mind appreciates the absence of humans and sees the Dhamma clearly and correctly.
passages.title: Dhammapada 373 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Suññāgāraṁ paviṭṭhassa,  santacittassa bhikkhuno;  Amānusī rati hoti,  sammā dhammaṁ vipassato.

passages.text: When one directly experiences the appearance and disappearance of the components of being, one acquires euphoria and joy, aware of the deathless.
passages.title: Dhammapada 374 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Yato yato sammasati,  khandhānaṁ udayabbayaṁ;  Labhatī pītipāmojjaṁ,  amataṁ taṁ vijānataṁ.

passages.text: This is the starting point for a monk: guarding the sense-faculties, contentment, and restraint according to the code of conduct.
passages.title: Dhammapada 375 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Tatrāyamādi bhavati,  idha paññassa bhikkhuno;  Indriyagutti santuṭṭhi,  pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro.

passages.text: If one associates with good spiritual friends who live a pure and diligent life, if one is polite in speech and wholesome in conduct, then one will have abundant joy and will put an end to suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 376 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe,  suddhājīve atandite;  Paṭisanthāravutyassa,  ācārakusalo siyā;  Tato pāmojjabahulo,  dukkhassantaṁ karissati.

passages.text: Just as a jasmine plant releases its wilted flowers, in the same way, monks, let go of your passion and aversion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 377 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Vassikā viya pupphāni,  maddavāni pamuñcati;  Evaṁ rāgañca dosañca,  vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.

passages.text: Peaceful in body, peaceful in speech, peaceful in mind, and well-concentrated, a monk who has expelled the world's bait is said to be at peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 378 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Santakāyo santavāco,  santavā susamāhito;  Vantalokāmiso bhikkhu,  “upasanto”ti vuccati.

passages.text: Admonish yourself, investigate yourself; a monk who is self-protected and mindful lives happily.
passages.title: Dhammapada 379 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Attanā codayattānaṁ,  paṭimaṁsetha attanā;  So attagutto satimā,  sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi.

passages.text: You are your own protector, for who could protect another? You are your own destiny; therefore, restrain yourself, as a merchant restrains an excellent horse.
passages.title: Dhammapada 380 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Attā hi attano nātho,  ko hi nātho paro siyā;  Attā hi attano gati,  tasmā saṁyamamattānaṁ;  Assaṁ bhadraṁva vāṇijo.

passages.text: A monk with abundant joy and serene faith in the Buddha's instructions arrives at the peaceful path and the happiness of complete tranquility.
passages.title: Dhammapada 381 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu,  pasanno buddhasāsane;  Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ,  saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: A young monk who makes a sincere effort in following the Buddha's instructions brightens this world, like the moon emerging from clouds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 382 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Monk Chapter
passages.original: Yo have daharo bhikkhu,  yuñjati buddhasāsane;  Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti,  abbhā muttova candimā.
