passages.text: Cut the stream, try to dispel sensuality, brahmin. Having known the elimination of all things, you will know the Unmade, brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 383 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma,  kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;  Saṅkhārānaṁ khayaṁ ñatvā,  akataññūsi brāhmaṇa.

passages.text: When a brahmin goes beyond duality, then all fetters come to an end for the one who knows.
passages.title: Dhammapada 384 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu,  pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo;  Athassa sabbe saṁyogā,  atthaṁ gacchanti jānato.

passages.text: One for whom the beyond, the not-beyond, and both beyond and not beyond cannot be found, without anxiety, unattached - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 385 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yassa pāraṁ apāraṁ vā,  pārāpāraṁ na vijjati;  Vītaddaraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Sitting dispassionately in meditation, the task complete, free of defilements, having reached the highest goal - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 386 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Jhāyiṁ virajamāsīnaṁ,  katakiccamanāsavaṁ;  Uttamatthamanuppattaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: The sun shines by day, the moon illuminates the night, a well-dressed aristocrat shines, a meditating brahmin shines, and the one that shines both day and night is the Buddha, the Radiant One.
passages.title: Dhammapada 387 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Divā tapati ādicco,  rattimābhāti candimā;  Sannaddho khattiyo tapati,  jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo;  Atha sabbamahorattiṁ,  buddho tapati tejasā.

passages.text: One who has expelled all evil is called a brahmin, one who lives peacefully is called a contemplative, one who has personally exiled all their contaminants is called a renunciant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 388 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Bāhitapāpoti brāhmaṇo,  Samacariyā samaṇoti vuccati;  Pabbājayamattano malaṁ,  Tasmā “pabbajito”ti vuccati.

passages.text: A brahmin would not attack another person, nor would a brahmin abandon one. Woe comes to one who attacks a brahmin, woe comes to one who abandons a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 389 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya,  nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo;  Dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṁ,  tato dhī yassa muñcati.

passages.text: There is nothing better than this for a brahmin: when the mind is kept away from its preferences. Whenever one turns away from causing harm, then suffering is replaced by peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 390 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Na brāhmaṇassetadakiñci seyyo,  Yadā nisedho manaso piyehi;  Yato yato hiṁsamano nivattati,  Tato tato sammatimeva dukkhaṁ.

passages.text: One who does no misconduct with body, speech, or mind, one who is restrained in these three ways - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 391 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yassa kāyena vācāya,  manasā natthi dukkaṭaṁ;  Saṁvutaṁ tīhi ṭhānehi,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: If someone has helped you understand the Dhamma taught by the fully awakened one, then you should respectfully venerate them, like a brahmin at a fire-sacrifice.
passages.title: Dhammapada 392 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yamhā dhammaṁ vijāneyya,  sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ;  Sakkaccaṁ taṁ namasseyya,  aggihuttaṁva brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: It is not because of tangled hair, lineage, or birth that one is a brahmin. One in whom there is truth, Dhamma, and purity is a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 393 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Na jaṭāhi na gottena,  na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo;  Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca,  so sucī so ca brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: Fool, what does tangled hair do for you? What does a goatskin robe do for you? Inside you there is a jungle; you only polish the outside.
passages.title: Dhammapada 394 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha,  kiṁ te ajinasāṭiyā;  Abbhantaraṁ te gahanaṁ,  bāhiraṁ parimajjasi.

passages.text: A person wearing rag-robes, lean, with protruding veins, meditating alone in the forest - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 395 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Paṁsukūladharaṁ jantuṁ,  kisaṁ dhamanisanthataṁ;  Ekaṁ vanasmiṁ jhāyantaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: I do not say that one is a brahmin because of the womb they were born from or the mother that produced them; if they are possessive; but one who is not possessive and not acquisitive - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 396 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Na cāhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ brūmi,  yonijaṁ mattisambhavaṁ;  sace hoti sakiñcano;  Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has cut all fetters and is not agitated, who has transcended all bonds and is unattached - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 397 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Sabbasaṁyojanaṁ chetvā,  yo ve na paritassati;  Saṅgātigaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Having cut the thong and strap, having broken every link of the chain, one who has removed the barricade and is awakened - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 398 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañca,  sandānaṁ sahanukkamaṁ;  Ukkhittapalighaṁ buddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Insult, attack, imprisonment - one who endures these without getting upset, with patience as strong as an army - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 399 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Akkosaṁ vadhabandhañca,  aduṭṭho yo titikkhati;  Khantībalaṁ balānīkaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Free from anger, religious, virtuous, humble, trained, bearing their final body - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 400 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Akkodhanaṁ vatavantaṁ,  sīlavantaṁ anussadaṁ;  Dantaṁ antimasārīraṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Like water on a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on a needle tip, one to whom sensuality does not stick - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 401 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Vāri pokkharapatteva,  āraggeriva sāsapo;  Yo na limpati kāmesu,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who understands suffering and has personally eliminated it here and now, who has set down the burden, unattached - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 402 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yo dukkhassa pajānāti,  idheva khayamattano;  Pannabhāraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has profound wisdom and intelligence, expert in what is and is not the path, who has attained the highest goal - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 403 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Gambhīrapaññaṁ medhāviṁ,  maggāmaggassa kovidaṁ;  Uttamatthamanuppattaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Not involved with laypeople or with monks, a homeless wanderer with few wishes - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 404 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Asaṁsaṭṭhaṁ gahaṭṭhehi,  anāgārehi cūbhayaṁ;  Anokasārimappicchaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has renounced violence towards living beings, whether weak or strong, who does not injure or kill - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 405 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Nidhāya daṇḍaṁ bhūtesu,  tasesu thāvaresu ca;  Yo na hanti na ghāteti,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who is unhindered amidst the hindered, self-disciplined, cooled, not acquisitive amidst the acquisitive - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 406 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Aviruddhaṁ viruddhesu,  attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṁ;  Sādānesu anādānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One from whom passion, hatred, conceit, and contempt have fallen away, like mustard seeds from a needle tip - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 407 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yassa rāgo ca doso ca,  māno makkho ca pātito;  Sāsaporiva āraggā,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who speaks words that are gentle, instructive, and true, and that do not create attachment to anything - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 408 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Akakkasaṁ viññāpaniṁ,  giraṁ saccamudīraye;  Yāya nābhisaje kañci,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who steals nothing in the world - whether it is long or short, small or large, beautiful or ugly - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 409 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā,  aṇuṁ thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ;  Loke adinnaṁ nādiyati,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One in whom no longing can be found, for this world or the next, free of longing, unattached - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 410 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Āsā yassa na vijjanti,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca;  Nirāsāsaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One in whom no adherence can be found, who has overcome confusion through direct knowledge, who has reached immersion in the deathless - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 411 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yassālayā na vijjanti,  aññāya akathaṅkathī;  Amatogadhamanuppattaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has transcended attachment to both merit and evil, sorrowless, immaculate, and pure - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 412 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yodha puññañca pāpañca,  ubho saṅgamupaccagā;  Asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who, like the moon, is stainless, pure, clear, and undisturbed; one who has completely eliminated delight in existence - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 413 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Candaṁva vimalaṁ suddhaṁ,  vippasannamanāvilaṁ;  Nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: This dangerous, difficult path, Saṁsāra, delusion - a meditator who has transcended it, crossed over it, gone beyond it, who is unmoved, unconfused, and enlightened through non-grasping - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 414 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yomaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ,  saṁsāraṁ mohamaccagā;  Tiṇṇo pāraṅgato jhāyī,  anejo akathaṅkathī;  Anupādāya nibbuto,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has abandoned sensuality, who wanders without a home, who has completely eliminated sensual existence - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 415 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yodha kāme pahantvāna,  anāgāro paribbaje;  Kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has abandoned craving, who wanders without a home, who has completely eliminated craving for existence - that is who I call a brahmin. One who has abandoned craving, who wanders without a home, who has completely eliminated craving for existence - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 416 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna,  anāgāro paribbaje;  Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.  Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna,  anāgāro paribbaje;  Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who is no longer attached to human existence, and is not attached to celestial existence either; one who is not attached to anything - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 417 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ,  dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā;  Sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Having relinquished liking and disliking, serene and non-possessive, a hero who has overcome the entire world - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 418 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Hitvā ratiñca aratiñca,  sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ;  Sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who completely understands the death and rebirth of sentient beings, unattached, heavenly, awake - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 419 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ,  upapattiñca sabbaso;  Asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One whose destiny is not known by any angel, spirit, or human, an Arahant whose corruptions have been eliminated - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 420 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yassa gatiṁ na jānanti,  devā gandhabbamānusā;  Khīṇāsavaṁ arahantaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who has nothing before, after, or in the middle; one who is not possessive and not acquisitive - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 421 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca,  majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṁ;  Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: A bull, an excellent hero, a great sage, a victor, unmoved, cleansed, awake - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 422 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ,  mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ;  Anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who knows their past lives, who sees heaven and hell, who has reached the elimination of birth, a sage who has mastery of higher knowledge, who has mastered every attainment - that is who I call a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 423 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · The Brahmin Chapter
passages.original: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedi,  saggāpāyañca passati;  Atho jātikkhayaṁ patto,  abhiññāvosito muni;  Sabbavositavosānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Who will investigate this earth, this world of death and angels? Who will collect the well-taught verses of truth, as a skilled florist collects flowers?
passages.title: Dhammapada 44 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Ko imaṁ pathaviṁ vicessati,  Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ;  Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ,  Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.

passages.text: A trainee will investigate this earth, this world of death and angels. A trainee will collect the well-taught verses of truth, as a skilled florist collects flowers.
passages.title: Dhammapada 45 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Sekho pathaviṁ vicessati,  Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ;  Sekho dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ,  Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.

passages.text: Having understood that this body is like foam, one who is aware that it is like a mirage, having cut Māra’s flower strands, goes where the Lord of Death does not see.
passages.title: Dhammapada 46 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā,  Marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno;  Chetvāna mārassa papupphakāni,  Adassanaṁ maccurājassa gacche.

passages.text: As if they were collecting flowers, a person collects mental attachments; like a sleeping village taken away by a great flood, they are taken away by death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 47 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ,  byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ;  Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova,  maccu ādāya gacchati.

passages.text: As if they were collecting flowers, a person collects mental attachments; never sated when it comes to sensuality, they are dominated by the Ender.
passages.title: Dhammapada 48 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ,  byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ;  Atittaññeva kāmesu,  antako kurute vasaṁ.

passages.text: Just as a bee takes nectar from a flower without harming its beauty or fragrance— a sage behaves the same way when in a village.
passages.title: Dhammapada 49 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi bhamaro pupphaṁ,  vaṇṇagandhamaheṭhayaṁ;  Paleti rasamādāya,  evaṁ gāme munī care.

passages.text: Do not look at the faults of others— what they have or have not done; Look only at yourself— what you have or have not done.
passages.title: Dhammapada 50 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Na paresaṁ vilomāni,  na paresaṁ katākataṁ;  Attanova avekkheyya,  katāni akatāni ca.

passages.text: Just like a lovely flower that has beauty but no fragrance, well-spoken words are fruitless when not acted out.
passages.title: Dhammapada 51 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ,  vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ;  Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā,  aphalā hoti akubbato.

passages.text: Just like a lovely flower that has both beauty and fragrance, well-spoken words are fruitful when acted out.
passages.title: Dhammapada 52 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ,  Vaṇṇavantaṁ sagandhakaṁ;  Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā,  Saphalā hoti kubbato.

passages.text: Just as one might make many garlands from a heap of flowers, in the same way, between birth and death one can do much that is wholesome.
passages.title: Dhammapada 53 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi puppharāsimhā,  kayirā mālāguṇe bahū;  Evaṁ jātena maccena,  kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.

passages.text: The fragrance of a flower does not go against the wind; nor does the fragrance of sandalwood, milkwood, or jasmine. However, the fragrance of goodness does go against the wind; a good person diffuses it in all directions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 54 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Na pupphagandho paṭivātameti,  Na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā;  Satañca gandho paṭivātameti,  Sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.

passages.text: Sandalwood or milkwood, lotus or jasmine, compared to these kinds of fragrances, the fragrance of virtue is unsurpassed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 55 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vāpi,  uppalaṁ atha vassikī;  Etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ,  sīlagandho anuttaro.

passages.text: The fragrance of milkwood and sandalwood is insignificant; the fragrance of virtue is the highest— it drifts amidst the angels.
passages.title: Dhammapada 56 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho,  yāyaṁ tagaracandanī;  Yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho,  vāti devesu uttamo.

passages.text: The path of those who have perfect virtue, live without negligence, and are liberated through right knowledge cannot be found by Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 57 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ,  appamādavihārinaṁ;  Sammadaññāvimuttānaṁ,  māro maggaṁ na vindati.

passages.text: Just as in a trash-heap discarded by the side of the road, a lotus might bloom— of pure fragrance and delightful to the mind—
passages.title: Dhammapada 58 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Yathā saṅkāradhānasmiṁ,  ujjhitasmiṁ mahāpathe;  Padumaṁ tattha jāyetha,  sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ.

passages.text: in the same way, amidst the trash-heap of beings— the blind commoners— a disciple of the Completely Awakened One outshines them with wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 59 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Flowers
passages.original: Evaṁ saṅkārabhūtesu,  andhabhūte puthujjane;  Atirocati paññāya,  sammāsambuddhasāvako.

passages.text: Long is the night for one who is awake, long is a yojana for one who is weary, long is saṁsāra for fools who do not understand the true Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 60 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Dīghā jāgarato ratti,  dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ;  Dīgho bālāna saṁsāro,  saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.

passages.text: If you do not find a traveler who is superior or equal to yourself, then resolutely travel alone; one cannot go with a fool.
passages.title: Dhammapada 61 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Carañce nādhigaccheyya,  Seyyaṁ sadisamattano;  Ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā,  Natthi bāle sahāyatā.

passages.text: A fool is tormented by thoughts of children and wealth; but since one does not even possess oneself, how could one possess children and wealth?
passages.title: Dhammapada 62 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Puttā matthi dhanaṁ matthi,  iti bālo vihaññati;  Attā hi attano natthi,  kuto puttā kuto dhanaṁ.

passages.text: A fool who conceives of foolishness is wise in that regard; but a fool who has the conceit of wisdom can truly be called a fool.
passages.title: Dhammapada 63 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ,  paṇḍito vāpi tena so;  Bālo ca paṇḍitamānī,  sa ve “bālo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: Even if a fool spends a lifetime in the presence of the wise, they do not understand the Dhamma, just as a spoon does not understand the flavor of soup.
passages.title: Dhammapada 64 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Yāvajīvampi ce bālo,  paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati;  Na so dhammaṁ vijānāti,  dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā.

passages.text: Even if a discerning person spends only a moment in the presence of the wise, they quickly understand the Dhamma, just as a tongue understands the flavor of soup.
passages.title: Dhammapada 65 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Muhuttamapi ce viññū,  paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati;  Khippaṁ dhammaṁ vijānāti,  jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.

passages.text: Unwise fools act as if they are not even their own friends— they perform evil actions which yield bitter fruit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 66 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Caranti bālā dummedhā,  amitteneva attanā;  Karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ,  yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.

passages.text: It is not good to perform an action which one will later regret, when, weeping with a tearful face, one experiences its result.
passages.title: Dhammapada 67 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu,  yaṁ katvā anutappati;  Yassa assumukho rodaṁ,  vipākaṁ paṭisevati.

passages.text: But it is good to perform an action which one will not later regret, when, satisfied and uplifted, one experiences its result.
passages.title: Dhammapada 68 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Tañca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu,  yaṁ katvā nānutappati;  Yassa patīto sumano,  vipākaṁ paṭisevati.

passages.text: A fool thinks that evil is sweet as long as its results have yet to fully manifest; but when the results of that evil fully manifest, then they descend into suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 69 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Madhuṁvā maññati bālo,  yāva pāpaṁ na paccati;  Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ,  atha dukkhaṁ nigacchati.

passages.text: Month after month a fool might eat using the tip of a blade of grass; but such a one is not worth even a sixteenth as much as those who comprehend the Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 70 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Māse māse kusaggena,  bālo bhuñjeyya bhojanaṁ;  Na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ,  kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ.

passages.text: Once an evil action has been performed, it is not released suddenly like milk; burning, it follows a fool, like fire concealed by ash.
passages.title: Dhammapada 71 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ,  Sajjukhīraṁva muccati;  Ḍahantaṁ bālamanveti,  Bhasmacchannova pāvako.

passages.text: It brings no benefit when fame comes to a fool; it destroys their good traits and tears apart their head.
passages.title: Dhammapada 72 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Yāvadeva anatthāya,  ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati;  Hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ,  muddhamassa vipātayaṁ.

passages.text: A fool wishes for a false existence— preeminence among monks, dominion in residences, and honor among other families.
passages.title: Dhammapada 73 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Asantaṁ bhāvanamiccheyya,  Purekkhārañca bhikkhusu;  Āvāsesu ca issariyaṁ,  Pūjaṁ parakulesu ca.

passages.text: “May both renunciants and laypeople think it was done by me alone; may I alone have the highest authority, in determining what should or should not be done.” In this way, the attitude, desire, and conceit of a fool grows.
passages.title: Dhammapada 74 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Mameva kata maññantu,  gihī pabbajitā ubho;  Mamevātivasā assu,  kiccākiccesu kismici;  Iti bālassa saṅkappo,  icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Knowledge is the cause of gain, knowledge leads to Nibbāna; since this is exactly what a monastic disciple of the Buddha understands, they do not delight in acclaim; they devote themselves to seclusion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 75 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Fools
passages.original: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā,  aññā nibbānagāminī;  Evametaṁ abhiññāya,  bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;  Sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya,  vivekamanubrūhaye.

passages.text: Like a person who leads you to hidden treasure: this is how to see a person who points out your faults. A wise person who tells you what you need to subdue is the kind of person you should associate with. Associating with that kind of person is always for the better and never for the worse.
passages.title: Dhammapada 76 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Nidhīnaṁva pavattāraṁ,  yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ;  Niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ,  tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje;  Tādisaṁ bhajamānassa,  seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.

passages.text: A person might advise you, instruct you, and keep you away from what is not good; They are liked by those who are good, and not liked by those who are not good.
passages.title: Dhammapada 77 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Ovadeyyānusāseyya,  asabbhā ca nivāraye;  Satañhi so piyo hoti,  asataṁ hoti appiyo.

passages.text: Do not associate with evil friends, do not associate with lowly people; associate with good spiritual friends and with the highest of people.
passages.title: Dhammapada 78 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Na bhaje pāpake mitte,  na bhaje purisādhame;  Bhajetha mitte kalyāṇe,  bhajetha purisuttame.

passages.text: When one enjoys the Dhamma, then one sleeps happily, with a clear mind; a wise person always appreciates the Dhamma proclaimed by the noble ones.
passages.title: Dhammapada 79 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Dhammapīti sukhaṁ seti,  vippasannena cetasā;  Ariyappavedite dhamme,  sadā ramati paṇḍito.

passages.text: Irrigators guide water, fletchers shape arrows, carpenters shape wood, the wise train themselves.
passages.title: Dhammapada 80 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā,  Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ;  Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā,  Attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.

passages.text: Just as the wind does not move solid stone, praise and criticism do not disturb the wise.
passages.title: Dhammapada 81 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Selo yathā ekaghano,  vātena na samīrati;  Evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu,  na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.

passages.text: Like a deep lake, clear and undisturbed, when the wise hear the Dhamma they attain clarity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 82 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Yathāpi rahado gambhīro,  vippasanno anāvilo;  Evaṁ dhammāni sutvāna,  vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.

passages.text: Good people let go of everything; the peaceful do not prattle about sensuality. Whether they are touched by pleasure or pain, neither elation nor depression can be seen in the wise.
passages.title: Dhammapada 83 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Sabbattha ve sappurisā cajanti,  Na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo;  Sukhena phuṭṭhā atha vā dukhena,  Na uccāvacaṁ paṇḍitā dassayanti.

passages.text: Whether because of oneself or because of another, one should not wish to obtain children, wealth, lordship, or personal success in ways contrary to Dhamma. Instead let one be virtuous, wise, and in accord with Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 84 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Na attahetu na parassa hetu,  Na puttamicche na dhanaṁ na raṭṭhaṁ;  Na iccheyya adhammena samiddhimattano,  Sa sīlavā paññavā dhammiko siyā.

passages.text: Few are the humans who go beyond. Most people only run around on the shore.
passages.title: Dhammapada 85 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Appakā te manussesu,  ye janā pāragāmino;  Athāyaṁ itarā pajā,  tīramevānudhāvati.

passages.text: Those who act in accordance with the well-explained Dhamma will go beyond the mortal realm so difficult to escape.
passages.title: Dhammapada 86 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte,  dhamme dhammānuvattino;  Te janā pāramessanti,  maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.

passages.text: Abandon dark things and develop bright things; a wise person leaves home for homelessness and lives in seclusion, where it is difficult to find satisfaction.
passages.title: Dhammapada 87 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya,  Sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito;  Okā anokamāgamma,  Viveke yattha dūramaṁ.

passages.text: One who has nothing could hope to find satisfaction there, after abandoning sensuality; a wise person would cleanse themselves of mental defilements.
passages.title: Dhammapada 88 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Tatrābhiratimiccheyya,  hitvā kāme akiñcano;  Pariyodapeyya attānaṁ,  cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

passages.text: Those who have developed the factors of awakening correctly and thoroughly, who have taken up relinquishment, who appreciate non-grasping, and have eliminated their corruptions— such radiant beings have attained Nibbāna in this world.
passages.title: Dhammapada 89 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on the Wise
passages.original: Yesaṁ sambodhiyaṅgesu,  sammā cittaṁ subhāvitaṁ;  Ādānapaṭinissagge,  anupādāya ye ratā;  Khīṇāsavā jutimanto,  te loke parinibbutā.

passages.text: In one who has completed the journey, is free of sorrow, has been completely liberated in every way, and has abandoned all ties, no fever can be found.
passages.title: Dhammapada 90 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Gataddhino visokassa,  vippamuttassa sabbadhi;  Sabbaganthappahīnassa,  pariḷāho na vijjati.

passages.text: Mindfully they strive upwards, they do not appreciate settling; Like swans leaving behind a lake, they abandon home after home.
passages.title: Dhammapada 91 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Uyyuñjanti satīmanto,  na nikete ramanti te;  Haṁsāva pallalaṁ hitvā,  okamokaṁ jahanti te.

passages.text: Those who have no stockpile, who have completely understood eating, whose domain is emptiness and objectless liberation— like birds in the sky, their movement is hard to follow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 92 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Yesaṁ sannicayo natthi,  ye pariññātabhojanā;  Suññato animitto ca,  vimokkho yesaṁ gocaro;  Ākāseva sakuntānaṁ,  gati tesaṁ durannayā.

passages.text: One who has completely eliminated their influences and is not dependent on consumption, whose domain is emptiness and objectless liberation— like birds in the sky, their path is hard to follow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 93 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Yassāsavā parikkhīṇā,  āhāre ca anissito;  Suññato animitto ca,  vimokkho yassa gocaro;  Ākāseva sakuntānaṁ,  padaṁ tassa durannayaṁ.

passages.text: One whose faculties are peaceful, like a horse well-trained by a charioteer, who has abandoned conceit and is free of influences, is envied even by the angels.
passages.title: Dhammapada 94 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Yassindriyāni samathaṅgatāni,  Assā yathā sārathinā sudantā;  Pahīnamānassa anāsavassa,  Devāpi tassa pihayanti tādino.

passages.text: One who, like the earth, opposes nothing, who is as stable as a pillar, practicing well, who is like a lake with no trace of mud— such beings are not reborn in saṁsāra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 95 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Pathavisamo no virujjhati,  Indakhilupamo tādi subbato;  Rahadova apetakaddamo,  Saṁsārā na bhavanti tādino.

passages.text: One whose mind is peaceful, whose speech and actions are peaceful, and who is liberated through right knowledge— such a person is at peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 96 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti,  santā vācā ca kamma ca;  Sammadaññāvimuttassa,  upasantassa tādino.

passages.text: One who is beyond faith, knows the Unmade, has severed all ties, has expelled defilement, and has rejected longing— this is truly the best person.
passages.title: Dhammapada 97 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Assaddho akataññū ca,  sandhicchedo ca yo naro;  Hatāvakāso vantāso,  sa ve uttamaporiso.

passages.text: Whether it is in a village or in the wilderness, in lowlands or highlands— any place where an arahant lives is a place worth appreciating.
passages.title: Dhammapada 98 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe,  Ninne vā yadi vā thale;  Yattha arahanto viharanti,  Taṁ bhūmirāmaṇeyyakaṁ.

passages.text: It is possible to appreciate the wilderness areas that most people do not appreciate; one who is free of passion will appreciate them, since they do not seek sensuality.
passages.title: Dhammapada 99 · Collection of Minor Texts · Verses of Dhamma · Chapter on Arahants
passages.original: Ramaṇīyāni araññāni,  yattha na ramatī jano;  Vītarāgā ramissanti,  na te kāmagavesino.

passages.text: 1 So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, “Mendicants!” “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Buddha said this: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sight that occupies a man’s mind like the sight of a woman. The sight of a woman occupies a man’s mind.” 2 “Mendicants, I do not see a single sound that occupies a man’s mind like the sound of a woman. The sound of a woman occupies a man’s mind.” 3 “Mendicants, I do not see a single smell that occupies a man’s mind like the smell of a woman. The smell of a woman occupies a man’s mind.” 4 “Mendicants, I do not see a single taste that occupies a man’s mind like the taste of a woman. The taste of a woman occupies a man’s mind.” 5 “Mendicants, I do not see a single touch that occupies a man’s mind like the touch of a woman. The touch of a woman occupies a man’s mind.” 6
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.1–10 · The Chapter on What Occupies the Mind
passages.original: 1  Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.  Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:  “bhikkhavo”ti.  “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.  Bhagavā etadavoca:  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarūpampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthirūpaṁ.  Itthirūpaṁ, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  2  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekasaddampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthisaddo.  Itthisaddo, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  3  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekagandhampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthigandho.  Itthigandho, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  4  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarasampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthiraso.  Itthiraso, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  5  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekaphoṭṭhabbampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthiphoṭṭhabbo.  Itthiphoṭṭhabbo, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  6

passages.text: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sight that occupies a woman’s mind like the sight of a man. The sight of a man occupies a woman’s mind.” 7 “Mendicants, I do not see a single sound that occupies a woman’s mind like the sound of a man. The sound of a man occupies a woman’s mind.” 8 “Mendicants, I do not see a single smell that occupies a woman’s mind like the smell of a man. The smell of a man occupies a woman’s mind.” 9 “Mendicants, I do not see a single taste that occupies a woman’s mind like the taste of a man. The taste of a man occupies a woman’s mind.” 10 “Mendicants, I do not see a single touch that occupies a woman’s mind like the touch of a man. The touch of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.1–10 · The Chapter on What Occupies the Mind
passages.original: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarūpampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisarūpaṁ.  Purisarūpaṁ, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  7  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekasaddampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisasaddo.  Purisasaddo, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  8  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekagandhampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisagandho.  Purisagandho, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  9  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarasampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisaraso.  Purisaraso, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.  10  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekaphoṭṭhabbampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisaphoṭṭhabbo.  Purisaphoṭṭhabbo, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.

passages.text: 11 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like the feature of beauty. When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of beauty, sensual desire arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.” 12 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like the feature of aversion. When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of aversion, ill will arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.” 13 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like discontent, sloth, yawning, sleepiness after eating, and mental sluggishness. When you have a sluggish mind, dullness and drowsiness arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.” 14 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to restlessness and remorse, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like an unsettled mind. When your mind is unsettled, restlessness and remorse arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.” 15
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.11–20 · The Chapter on Giving Up the Hindrances
passages.original: 11  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā kāmacchando uppajjati uppanno vā kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, subhanimittaṁ.  Subhanimittaṁ, bhikkhave, ayoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.  12  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā byāpādo uppajjati uppanno vā byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭighanimittaṁ.  Paṭighanimittaṁ, bhikkhave, ayoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.  13  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ uppajjati uppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, arati tandī vijambhitā bhattasammado cetaso ca līnattaṁ.  Līnacittassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṁ uppajjati uppannañca thinamiddhaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.  14  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ uppajjati uppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cetaso avūpasamo.  Avūpasantacittassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṁ uppajjati uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.  15

passages.text: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like irrational application of mind. When you apply the mind irrationally, doubt arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.” 16 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents sensual desire from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like the feature of ugliness. When you apply the mind rationally to the feature of ugliness, sensual desire does not arise, or, if it has already arisen, it’s given up.” 17 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents ill will from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like the heart’s release by love. When you apply the mind rationally to the heart’s release by love, ill will does not arise, or, if it has already arisen, it’s given up.” 18 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents dullness and drowsiness from arising, or, when they have arisen, gives them up like the elements of initiative, persistence, and vigor. When you’re energetic, dullness and drowsiness do not arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re given up.” 19
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.11–20 · The Chapter on Giving Up the Hindrances
passages.original: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā vicikicchā uppajjati uppannā vā vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, ayonisomanasikāro.  Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasi karoto anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.  16  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā kāmacchando nuppajjati uppanno vā kāmacchando pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, asubhanimittaṁ.  Asubhanimittaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando nuppajjati uppanno ca kāmacchando pahīyatī”ti.  17  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā byāpādo nuppajjati uppanno vā byāpādo pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, mettā cetovimutti.  Mettaṁ, bhikkhave, cetovimuttiṁ yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva byāpādo nuppajjati uppanno ca byāpādo pahīyatī”ti.  18  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ nuppajjati uppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, ārambhadhātu nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu.  Āraddhavīriyassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṁ nuppajjati uppannañca thinamiddhaṁ pahīyatī”ti.  19

passages.text: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents restlessness and remorse from arising, or, when they have arisen, gives them up like a settled mind. When the mind is settled, restlessness and remorse do not arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re given up.” 20 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents doubt from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like rational application of mind. When you apply the mind rationally, doubt does not arise, or, if it’s already arisen, it’s given up.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.11–20 · The Chapter on Giving Up the Hindrances
passages.original: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ nuppajjati uppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cetaso vūpasamo.  Vūpasantacittassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṁ nuppajjati uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīyatī”ti.  20  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā vicikicchā nuppajjati uppannā vā vicikicchā pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, yonisomanasikāro.  Yoniso, bhikkhave, manasi karoto anuppannā ceva vicikicchā nuppajjati uppannā ca vicikicchā pahīyatī”ti.

passages.text: 140 “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain what is not the teaching as not the teaching are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.” 141 “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain what is the teaching as the teaching are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.” 142–149 “Those mendicants who explain what is not found in the monastic law as not found in the monastic law … what is found in the monastic law as found in the monastic law … what was not spoken and stated by the Realized One as not spoken and stated by the Realized One … what was spoken and stated by the Realized One as spoken and stated by the Realized One … what was not practiced by the Realized One as not practiced by the Realized One … what was practiced by the Realized One as practiced by the Realized One … what was not prescribed by the Realized One as not prescribed by the Realized One … what was prescribed by the Realized One as prescribed by the Realized One … are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.140–149 · The Chapter on Not the Teaching
passages.original: 140  “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū adhammaṁ adhammoti dīpenti te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.  Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū puññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ ṭhapentī”ti.  141  “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dhammaṁ dhammoti dīpenti te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.  Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū puññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ ṭhapentī”ti.  142–149  “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū avinayaṁ avinayoti dīpenti …pe… vinayaṁ vinayoti dīpenti …pe… abhāsitaṁ alapitaṁ tathāgatena abhāsitaṁ alapitaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpenti …pe… bhāsitaṁ lapitaṁ tathāgatena bhāsitaṁ lapitaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpenti …pe… anāciṇṇaṁ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpenti …pe… āciṇṇaṁ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpenti …pe… apaññattaṁ tathāgatena apaññattaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpenti …pe… paññattaṁ tathāgatena paññattaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpenti;  te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.  Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū puññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ ṭhapentī”ti.

passages.text: 150 “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain a non-offense as an offense are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans. They brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.” 151 “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain an offense as a non-offense are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans. Those mendicants brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.” 152–159 “Those mendicants who explain a light offense as a heavy offense … a heavy offense as a light offense … a grave offense as a minor offense … a minor offense as a grave offense … a curable offense as an incurable offense … an incurable offense as a curable offense … an offense requiring amends as an offense not requiring amends … an offense not requiring amends as an offense requiring amends are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans. Those mendicants brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.” 160

passages.text: 170 “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. What one individual? The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.” 171 “The appearance of one individual, mendicants, is rare in the world. What one individual? The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. This is the one individual, mendicants, whose appearance is rare in the world.” 172 “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world who is an incredible human being. What one individual? The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world who is an incredible human being.” 173
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.170–187 · The Chapter on One Individual
passages.original: 170  “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.  Katamo ekapuggalo?  Tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.  Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.  171  “Ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ.  Katamassa ekapuggalassa?  Tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa.  Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin”ti.  172  “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso.  Katamo ekapuggalo?  Tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.  Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso”ti.  173

passages.text: “The death of one individual, mendicants, is regretted by many people. What one individual? The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. This is the one individual, mendicants, whose death is regretted by many people.” 174 “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world unique, without peer or rival, incomparable, matchless, unrivaled, unequaled, without equal, the best of men. What one individual? The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world unique, without peer or rival, incomparable, matchless, unrivaled, unequaled, without equal, the best of men.” 175–186 “With the appearance of one individual, mendicants, there is the appearance of a great eye, a great light, a great radiance, and the six unsurpassable things; the realization of the four kinds of textual analysis; the penetration of many and diverse elements; the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom; the realization of the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection. What one individual? The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. This is the one individual whose appearance brings the appearance of a great eye, a great light, a great radiance, and the six unsurpassable things; the realization of the four kinds of textual analysis; the penetration of many and diverse elements; the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom; the realization of the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.” 187
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.170–187 · The Chapter on One Individual
passages.original: “Ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, kālakiriyā bahuno janassa anutappā hoti.  Katamassa ekapuggalassa?  Tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa.  Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalassa kālakiriyā bahuno janassa anutappā hotī”ti.  174  “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati adutiyo asahāyo appaṭimo appaṭisamo appaṭibhāgo appaṭipuggalo asamo asamasamo dvipadānaṁ aggo.  Katamo ekapuggalo?  Tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.  Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati adutiyo asahāyo appaṭimo appaṭisamo appaṭibhāgo appaṭipuggalo asamo asamasamo dvipadānaṁ aggo”ti.  175–186  “Ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvā mahato cakkhussa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato ālokassa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato obhāsassa pātubhāvo hoti, channaṁ anuttariyānaṁ pātubhāvo hoti, catunnaṁ paṭisambhidānaṁ sacchikiriyā hoti, anekadhātupaṭivedho hoti, nānādhātupaṭivedho hoti, vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, arahattaphalasacchikiriyā hoti.  Katamassa ekapuggalassa?  Tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa.  Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalassa pātubhāvā mahato cakkhussa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato ālokassa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato obhāsassa pātubhāvo hoti, channaṁ anuttariyānaṁ pātubhāvo hoti, catunnaṁ paṭisambhidānaṁ sacchikiriyā hoti, anekadhātupaṭivedho hoti, nānādhātupaṭivedho hoti, vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, arahattaphalasacchikiriyā hotī”ti.  187

passages.text: “Mendicants, I do not see a single other individual who rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One like Sāriputta. Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.170–187 · The Chapter on One Individual
passages.original: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekapuggalampi samanupassāmi yo evaṁ tathāgatena anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattitaṁ sammadeva anuppavatteti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, sāriputto.  Sāriputto, bhikkhave, tathāgatena anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattitaṁ sammadeva anuppavattetī”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my monk disciples in long standing is Koṇḍañña Who Understood.” “… with great wisdom is Sāriputta.” “… with psychic power is Mahāmoggallāna.” “… who advocate austerities is Mahākassapa.” “… with clairvoyance is Anuruddha.” “… from eminent families is Bhaddiya son of Kāḷīgodhā.” “… with a charming voice is Bhaddiya the Dwarf.” “… with a lion’s roar is Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer.” “… who speak on the teaching is Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī.” “… who explain in detail the meaning of a brief statement is Mahākaccāna.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.188–197 · Chapter One
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ rattaññūnaṁ yadidaṁ aññāsikoṇḍañño.  … Mahāpaññānaṁ yadidaṁ sāriputto.  … Iddhimantānaṁ yadidaṁ mahāmoggallāno.  … Dhutavādānaṁ yadidaṁ mahākassapo.  … Dibbacakkhukānaṁ yadidaṁ anuruddho.  … Uccākulikānaṁ yadidaṁ bhaddiyo kāḷigodhāya putto.  … Mañjussarānaṁ yadidaṁ lakuṇḍaka bhaddiyo.  … Sīhanādikānaṁ yadidaṁ piṇḍolabhāradvājo.  … Dhammakathikānaṁ yadidaṁ puṇṇo mantāṇiputto.  … saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajantānaṁ yadidaṁ mahākaccāno”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my monk disciples in creating a mind-made body is Cūḷapanthaka.” “… who are skilled in the turning away of the mind is Cūḷapanthaka.” “… who are skilled in the turning away through perception is Mahāpanthaka.” “… who live without strife is Subhūti.” “… who are worthy of a religious donation is Subhūti.” “… who stay in the wilderness is Revata of the Acacia Wood.” “… who practice absorption is Revata the Doubter.” “… who are energetic is Soṇa Koḷivisa.” “… who enunciate well is Soṇa of the Sharp Ears.” “… who receive many possessions is Sīvali.” “… who are committed to faith is Vakkalī.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.198–208 · Chapter Two
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ abhinimminantānaṁ yadidaṁ cūḷapanthako.  … Cetovivaṭṭakusalānaṁ yadidaṁ cūḷapanthako.  … Saññāvivaṭṭakusalānaṁ yadidaṁ mahāpanthako.  … Araṇavihārīnaṁ yadidaṁ subhūti.  … Dakkhiṇeyyānaṁ yadidaṁ subhūti.  … Āraññakānaṁ yadidaṁ revato khadiravaniyo.  … Jhāyīnaṁ yadidaṁ kaṅkhārevato.  … Āraddhavīriyānaṁ yadidaṁ soṇo koḷiviso.  … Kalyāṇavākkaraṇānaṁ yadidaṁ soṇo kuṭikaṇṇo.  … Lābhīnaṁ yadidaṁ sīvali.  … Saddhādhimuttānaṁ yadidaṁ vakkalī”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my monk disciples who want to train is Rāhula.” “… who went forth out of faith is Raṭṭhapāla.” “… who are the first to vote is Kuṇḍadhāna.” “… who are eloquent poets is Vaṅgīsa.” “… who are impressive all around is Upasena son of Vaṅgantā.” “… who assign lodgings is Dabba the Mallian.” “… who are beloved of the deities is Pilindavaccha.” “… with swift insight is Bāhiya of the Bark Cloth.” “… with brilliant speech is Kassapa the Prince.” “… who have attained the methods of textual analysis is Mahākoṭṭhita.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.209–218 · Chapter Three
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhākāmānaṁ yadidaṁ rāhulo.  … Saddhāpabbajitānaṁ yadidaṁ raṭṭhapālo.  … Paṭhamaṁ salākaṁ gaṇhantānaṁ yadidaṁ kuṇḍadhāno.  … Paṭibhānavantānaṁ yadidaṁ vaṅgīso.  … Samantapāsādikānaṁ yadidaṁ upaseno vaṅgantaputto.  … Senāsanapaññāpakānaṁ yadidaṁ dabbo mallaputto.  … devatānaṁ piyamanāpānaṁ yadidaṁ pilindavaccho.  … Khippābhiññānaṁ yadidaṁ bāhiyo dārucīriyo.  … Cittakathikānaṁ yadidaṁ kumārakassapo.  … Paṭisambhidāpattānaṁ yadidaṁ mahākoṭṭhito”ti.

passages.text: 21 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so unworkable as this mind that is not developed. An undeveloped mind is unworkable.” 22 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so workable as this mind that is developed A developed mind is workable.” 23 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed. An undeveloped mind is very harmful.” 24 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed. A developed mind is very beneficial.” 25 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed or manifested. An undeveloped and unmanifested mind is very harmful.” 26 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed and manifested. A developed and manifested mind is very beneficial.” 27 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed and cultivated. An undeveloped and uncultivated mind is very harmful.” 28
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.21–30 · The Chapter on the Unworkable
passages.original: 21  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ akammaniyaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ akammaniyaṁ hotī”ti.  22  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ kammaniyaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ kammaniyaṁ hotī”ti.  23  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.  24  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.  25  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ apātubhūtaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ apātubhūtaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.  26  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ pātubhūtaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ pātubhūtaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.  27  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.  28

passages.text: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed and cultivated. A developed and cultivated mind is very beneficial.” 29 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that brings such suffering as this mind that is not developed and cultivated. An undeveloped and uncultivated mind brings suffering.” 30 “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that brings such happiness as this mind that is developed and cultivated. A developed and cultivated mind brings happiness.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.21–30 · The Chapter on the Unworkable
passages.original: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.  29  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ dukkhādhivahaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ dukkhādhivahaṁ hotī”ti.  30  “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ sukhādhivahaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.  Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ sukhādhivahaṁ hotī”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my monk disciples who are very learned is Ānanda.” “… in memory is Ānanda.” “… in rememberance is Ānanda.” “… in retention is Ānanda.” “… as a personal attendant is Ānanda.” “… with a large congregation is Kassapa of Uruvelā.” “… who impress lay families is Kāḷudāyī.” “… with good health is Bakkula.” “… who recollect past lives is Sobhita.” “… who have memorized the monastic law is Upāli.” “… who advise the nuns is Nandaka.” “… who guard the sense doors is Nanda.” “… who advise the monks is Mahākappina.” “… who are skilled in the fire element is Sāgata.” “… who inspire eloquent teachings is Rādha.” “… who wear coarse robes is Mogharāja.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.219–234 · Chapter Four
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahussutānaṁ yadidaṁ ānando.  … Satimantānaṁ yadidaṁ ānando.  … Gatimantānaṁ yadidaṁ ānando.  … Dhitimantānaṁ yadidaṁ ānando.  … Upaṭṭhākānaṁ yadidaṁ ānando.  … Mahāparisānaṁ yadidaṁ uruvelakassapo.  … Kulappasādakānaṁ yadidaṁ kāḷudāyī.  … Appābādhānaṁ yadidaṁ bākulo.  … Pubbenivāsaṁ anussarantānaṁ yadidaṁ sobhito.  … Vinayadharānaṁ yadidaṁ upāli.  … Bhikkhunovādakānaṁ yadidaṁ nandako.  … Indriyesu guttadvārānaṁ yadidaṁ nando.  … Bhikkhuovādakānaṁ yadidaṁ mahākappino.  … Tejodhātukusalānaṁ yadidaṁ sāgato.  … Paṭibhāneyyakānaṁ yadidaṁ rādho.  … Lūkhacīvaradharānaṁ yadidaṁ mogharājā”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my nun disciples in long standing is Mahāpajāpati Gotamī.” “… with great wisdom is Khemā.” “… with psychic power is Uppalavaṇṇā.” “… who have memorized the monastic law is Paṭācārā.” “… who speak on the teaching is Dhammadinnā.” “… who practice absorption is Nandā.” “… who are energetic is Soṇā.” “… with clairvoyance is Sakulā.” “… with swift insight is Bhaddā of the Curly Hair.” “… who recollect past lives is Bhaddā daughter of Kapila.” “… who have attained great insight is Bhaddakaccānā.” “… who wear coarse robes is Kisāgotamī.” “… who are committed to faith is Sigālaka’s Mother.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.235–247 · Chapter Five
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvikānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ rattaññūnaṁ yadidaṁ mahāpajāpatigotamī.  … Mahāpaññānaṁ yadidaṁ khemā.  … Iddhimantīnaṁ yadidaṁ uppalavaṇṇā.  … Vinayadharānaṁ yadidaṁ paṭācārā.  … Dhammakathikānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammadinnā.  … Jhāyīnaṁ yadidaṁ nandā.  … Āraddhavīriyānaṁ yadidaṁ soṇā.  … Dibbacakkhukānaṁ yadidaṁ bakulā.  … Khippābhiññānaṁ yadidaṁ bhaddā kuṇḍalakesā.  … Pubbenivāsaṁ anussarantīnaṁ yadidaṁ bhaddā kāpilānī.  … Mahābhiññāpattānaṁ yadidaṁ bhaddakaccānā.  … Lūkhacīvaradharānaṁ yadidaṁ kisāgotamī.  … Saddhādhimuttānaṁ yadidaṁ siṅgālakamātā”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my laymen disciples in first going for refuge are the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika.” “… as a donor is the householder Sudatta Anāthapiṇḍika.” “… who speak on the teaching is the householder Citta of Macchikāsaṇḍika.” “… who attract a congregation by the four ways of being inclusive is Hatthaka of Āḷavī.” “… who donate fine things is Mahānāma the Sakyan.” “… who donate nice things is the householder Ugga of Vesālī.” “… who attend on the Saṅgha is the householder Uggata of Elephant Village.” “… who have experiential confidence is Sūra Ambaṭṭha.” “… who have confidence in an individual is Jīvaka Komārabhacca.” “… who are trusting is the householder Nakula’s father.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.248–257 · Chapter Six
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ paṭhamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchantānaṁ yadidaṁ tapussabhallikā vāṇijā.  … Dāyakānaṁ yadidaṁ sudatto gahapati anāthapiṇḍiko.  … Dhammakathikānaṁ yadidaṁ citto gahapati macchikāsaṇḍiko.  … Catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi parisaṁ saṅgaṇhantānaṁ yadidaṁ hatthako āḷavako.  … Paṇītadāyakānaṁ yadidaṁ mahānāmo sakko.  … Manāpadāyakānaṁ yadidaṁ uggo gahapati vesāliko.  … Saṅghupaṭṭhākānaṁ yadidaṁ hatthigāmako uggato gahapati.  … Aveccappasannānaṁ yadidaṁ sūrambaṭṭho.  … Puggalappasannānaṁ yadidaṁ jīvako komārabhacco.  … Vissāsakānaṁ yadidaṁ nakulapitā gahapatī”ti.

passages.text: “The foremost of my laywomen disciples in first going for refuge is Sujātā of the town of Senā.” “… as a donor is Visākhā, Migāra’s mother.” “… who are very learned is Khujjuttarā.” “… who dwell in love is Sāmāvatī.” “… who practice absorption is Uttarā, Nanda’s mother.” “… who give fine things is Suppavāsā the Koliyan.” “… who care for the sick is the laywoman Suppiyā.” “… who have experiential confidence is Kātiyānī.” “… who are trusting is the housewife Nakula’s mother.” “… whose confidence is based on oral transmission is the laywoman Kāḷī of Kuraraghara.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.258–267 · Chapter Seven
passages.original: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvikānaṁ upāsikānaṁ paṭhamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchantīnaṁ yadidaṁ sujātā seniyadhītā.  … Dāyikānaṁ yadidaṁ visākhā migāramātā.  … Bahussutānaṁ yadidaṁ khujjuttarā.  … Mettāvihārīnaṁ yadidaṁ sāmāvatī.  … Jhāyīnaṁ yadidaṁ uttarānandamātā.  … Paṇītadāyikānaṁ yadidaṁ suppavāsā koliyadhītā.  … Gilānupaṭṭhākīnaṁ yadidaṁ suppiyā upāsikā.  … Aveccappasannānaṁ yadidaṁ kātiyānī.  … Vissāsikānaṁ yadidaṁ nakulamātā gahapatānī.  … Anussavappasannānaṁ yadidaṁ kāḷī upāsikā kuraragharikā”ti.

passages.text: 268 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take any condition as permanent. That is not possible. But it is possible for an ordinary person to take some condition as permanent. That is possible.” 269 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take any condition as pleasant. But it is possible for an ordinary person to take some condition as pleasant.” 270 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take anything as self. But it is possible for an ordinary person to take something as self.” 271 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder their mother. But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder their mother.” 272 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder their father. But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder their father.” 273
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.268–277 · Chapter One
passages.original: 268  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṁ niccato upagaccheyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṁ niccato upagaccheyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  269  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṁ sukhato upagaccheyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṁ sukhato upagaccheyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  270  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci dhammaṁ attato upagaccheyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano kañci dhammaṁ attato upagaccheyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  271  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo mātaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano mātaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  272  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo pitaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano pitaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  273

passages.text: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder a perfected one. But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder a perfected one.” 274 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to injure a Realized One with malicious intent. But it is possible for an ordinary person to injure a Realized One with malicious intent.” 275 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to cause a schism in the Saṅgha. But it is possible for an ordinary person to cause a schism in the Saṅgha.” 276 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to dedicate themselves to another teacher. But it is possible for an ordinary person to dedicate themselves to another teacher.” 277 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for two perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas to arise in the same solar system at the same time. But it is possible for just one perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, to arise in one solar system.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.268–277 · Chapter One
passages.original: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo arahantaṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano arahantaṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  274  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo tathāgatassa paduṭṭhacitto lohitaṁ uppādeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano tathāgatassa paduṭṭhacitto lohitaṁ uppādeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  275  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo saṅghaṁ bhindeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano saṅghaṁ bhindeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  276  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo aññaṁ satthāraṁ uddiseyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano aññaṁ satthāraṁ uddiseyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  277  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṁ acarimaṁ uppajjeyyuṁ. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā ekova arahaṁ sammāsambuddho uppajjeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.

passages.text: 278 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for two wheel-turning monarchs to arise in the same solar system at the same time. But it is possible for just one wheel-turning monarch to arise in one solar system.” 279 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to be a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha. But it is possible for a man to be a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.” 280 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to be a wheel-turning monarch. But it is possible for a man to be a wheel-turning monarch.” 281–283 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to perform the role of Sakka, Māra, or the Divinity. But it is possible for a man to perform the role of Sakka, Māra, or the Divinity.” 284 “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from bad bodily conduct. But it is possible for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from bad bodily conduct.” 285–286
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.278–286 · Chapter Two
passages.original: 278  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve rājāno cakkavattī apubbaṁ acarimaṁ uppajjeyyuṁ. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā eko rājā cakkavattī uppajjeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  279  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ itthī arahaṁ assa sammāsambuddho. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho, etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puriso arahaṁ assa sammāsambuddho. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  280  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puriso rājā assa cakkavattī. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  281–283  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ itthī sakkattaṁ kāreyya …pe… mārattaṁ kāreyya …pe… brahmattaṁ kāreyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puriso sakkattaṁ kāreyya …pe… mārattaṁ kāreyya …pe… brahmattaṁ kāreyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  284  “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ kāyaduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ kāyaduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.  285–286

passages.text: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from bad verbal … bad mental conduct. But it is possible for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from bad verbal … bad mental conduct.”
passages.title: Numbered Discourses 1.278–286 · Chapter Two
passages.original: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ vacīduccaritassa …pe… yaṁ manoduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.  Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ manoduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
